Rinit.doc:
Starts the library with default settings on the given backend.
The calling thread becomes the UI thread.
Returns R_TRUE on success. On failure, see Rerror_get_last.

Rinit_ex.doc:
Starts the library with explicit settings.
Settings, or NULL for the defaults.

Rshutdown.doc:
Destroys every window, widget and resource, stops the worker and
render threads and releases the backend.

Rset_allocator.doc:
Replaces the allocator of Raven with the functions of the
application (an engine allocator, a tracker...). NULL selects the
allocator of Raven again. Must be called before Rinit, and before any
other function that allocates. The functions are called from several
threads; alloc must return memory aligned for any type (16 bytes).

Rallocator_get_system.doc:
Returns An allocator that forwards to malloc, realloc and free of the C
runtime: Rset_allocator(Rallocator_get_system()) is how memory tools
that follow malloc (Valgrind, heap profilers) see the blocks of Raven.
The environment variable RAVEN_ALLOCATOR=system does the same without
recompiling, and it is the default in a build with AddressSanitizer.

Rmemory_alloc.doc:
Memory from the allocator of Raven (or from the one given to
Rset_allocator), for the application: custom widgets, pixel buffers.
Aligned on 16 bytes. Never returns NULL: running out of memory is a
fatal error. Thread-safe.

Rmemory_realloc.doc: Resizes a block, keeping its content. A NULL block is allocated. Thread-safe.

Rmemory_free.doc: Frees a block. NULL is ignored. Thread-safe.

Rmemory_get_stats.doc: What the library holds right now. Thread-safe.

Rmemory_check.doc:
Walks the whole heap of Raven and verifies its structure.
Returns R_FALSE when it is corrupted (a buffer overrun wrote over a block
header). Slow: for tests and for hunting a bug. Thread-safe.

Rmemory_trim.doc: Returns to the OS the regions of the heap that hold nothing. Thread-safe.

Rdraw_frame.doc:
Produces one frame: processes the pending OS events without
waiting, runs the posted tasks and the timers, then lays out, paints and
submits every window that changed. A window in which nothing changed is
not drawn again, so the call is cheap when the UI is idle.
Returns R_FALSE once Rquit was called or the last window is closed.

Rwait_frame.doc:
Same as Rdraw_frame, but first sleeps until there is something to
do: an OS event, a posted task, a timer, an animation, a pending redraw.
Longest sleep. Negative sleeps without limit, 0
does not sleep.

Rquit.doc: Makes Rdraw_frame and Rwait_frame return R_FALSE. Thread-safe.

Rget_exit_code.doc: Returns The code given to Rquit, 0 when the last window was closed.

Ris_running.doc: Returns R_FALSE once Rquit was called or every window is closed.

Rpoll_events.doc:
Processes the pending OS events without producing a frame.
Rdraw_frame does it already: only useful to keep the windows responsive
during a long operation.

Rwait_events.doc:
Sleeps until an OS event, a posted task, a timer or a pending
redraw, and processes the OS events. Rwait_frame does it already.
Maximum wait. Negative waits without limit.

Rget_delta_time.doc: Returns Seconds between the last two frames.

Rget_time.doc: Returns Seconds elapsed since Rinit, from a monotonic clock. Thread-safe.

Ris_app_paused.doc: Returns R_TRUE between R_APP_DID_PAUSE and R_APP_WILL_RESUME: the application is in the background.

Rinject_app_event.doc:
Handles an RAppEvent as if the system had sent it: for tests,
and for a host application (raven_host.h) that knows the lifecycle.
UI thread.

Rset_ui_scale.doc:
Scale of the whole interface, on top of the one of the monitor
(RInitDesc.ui_scale at start): every window is laid out again. 0.25 .. 4.

Rset_vsync.doc:
R_TRUE: every frame waits for the vertical synchronization of the
screen (no tearing, no wasted frames); R_FALSE: as fast as possible
(RInitDesc.disable_vsync at start). Takes effect at the next frame.

Rset_animations_enabled.doc:
R_FALSE makes every change immediate: for users who ask for
reduced motion (Raccessibility_set_reduce_motion), and for tests that
read the state right after an input.

Rset_animation_speed.doc: Multiplies the speed of every animation. 1 is the default, 0.25 a slow motion.

Rset_animation_time_step.doc:
When positive, each frame advances the animations by exactly this
many seconds instead of the time really elapsed: frames rendered one by
one for a video or a screenshot, deterministic tests. 0 follows the clock.

Rtask_post.doc:
Queues a function to run on the UI thread during the next frame
and wakes Rwait_frame. Thread-safe: this is how worker threads touch the UI.

Rtask_run_async.doc: Runs a function on a worker thread of the job system. Thread-safe.

Rparallel_for.doc:
Splits [0, count) into ranges of at most `grain` items and runs them
on the worker threads and the calling thread. Returns when all are done.

Rwake_up.doc: Wakes Rwait_frame and Rwait_events from any thread.

Rtimer_create.doc:
Calls a function on the UI thread after `interval_seconds`.
R_TRUE to fire repeatedly, R_FALSE to fire once and delete itself.

Raction_fire.doc:
Fires an action as a widget would: the function bound to the
name is called, or the default handler. What a tool bar button, a
script or a test uses to do what a menu item does.
Passed to the function; R_INVALID_ID when there is none.

Raction_set_default_handler.doc: Receives every action that has no bound function and is not one of the built-in actions (e.g. a script bridge).

Raction_get_sender.doc: Returns The widget whose event fired the action, R_INVALID_ID when a script calls it.

Raction_get_argument_count.doc: Returns The number of arguments given: the parameters of the signature, fewer when an event gives fewer... never more.

Raction_get_number.doc: The arguments, by position from 0. A wrong index or type reports an error and gives 0, "" or R_FALSE.

Raction_get_string.doc: Returns Valid until the function returns.

Raction_return_number.doc: The value returned to the script; of the type of the signature (what is set last counts).

Raction_fail.doc:
The function failed: the script that called it stops with error
RS205 and this message (the application goes on; so does the next event).

Raction_set_builtins.doc:
The actions Raven knows by itself: an interface written in XML
uses them with no C at all (OnClicked="app.quit").

app.quit                          quits (Rquit(0))
window.close, window.minimize,    the window of the widget
window.maximize, window.restore   (maximize goes back when it already is)
window.picture_in_picture         in and out of picture in picture
island.expand, island.fold,       the island of that window
island.toggle
theme.dark, theme.light,          the look of Raven, dark or light
theme.toggle
theme:NAME                        Rtheme_use(NAME): a theme loaded or built in
language:CODE                     Rlocale_set_language(CODE)
open:ADDRESS                      Ropen_url (https:, mailto:, a file)
copy:TEXT                         the text to the clipboard
show:NAME, hide:NAME, toggle:NAME the widget named NAME in the window (hidden: Collapsed)
enable:NAME, disable:NAME
focus:NAME
page:NAME=2, page:NAME=+1         what a Switcher, a TabView, a ComboBox or a ListView
shows; +1 and -1 step, and go round

A function bound to one of these names (Raction_bind) replaces it; the
default handler receives the others only.
R_FALSE turns them all off: a design tool that shows
interfaces without running them. On by default.

Raction_is_builtin.doc: Returns R_TRUE when the name is one of the built-in actions (Raction_set_builtins), whether they are on or not.

Ropen_url.doc:
Opens an address with the program the user has for it: a web
page in the browser, a mailto: in the mail program, a file in its
application. Returns at once.
Returns R_FALSE when the OS could not be asked (nothing tells whether
a program then really opened it).

Rclipboard_set_html.doc:
Copies one content in two formats: `html` for the programs that
paste formatting (word processors, chat, mail) and `text` for the
others (editors, terminals). Each program takes the format it prefers.
Where the window system has no clipboard formats (Win32 and macOS for
now), or `html` is NULL, it is Rclipboard_set_text(text).

Rclipboard_get_text.doc: Returns The clipboard text, or "" when empty. Valid until the next call.

Rerror_get_last.doc:
Retrieves and clears the last recorded error.
Optional output: human-readable description.
Optional output: severity of the error.
Returns R_NO_ERROR when nothing was recorded.

Rwindow_create.doc:
Opens a top-level window.
Client size in logical units.
Bitmask of RWindowFlags.

Rwindow_destroy.doc: Closes a window and deletes its content widgets.

Rwindow_set_content.doc:
Sets the root widget of the window. The window takes ownership of
the widget; the previous content is deleted.

Rwindow_get_safe_area.doc:
The part of the window the system covers (status bar, notch,
home indicator, navigation bar), in logical units. The content of the
window is laid out inside it already. All 0 on desktop.

Rwindow_get_keyboard_area.doc:
The part of the window the on-screen keyboard covers (only
`bottom` is set), in logical units; 0 when it is hidden or there is
none (desktop). The content is laid out above it already, and the
field that has the focus is scrolled into view above it, by the
ScrollBoxes that hold it, when the keyboard comes or changes height,
when the window turns, and when another field takes the focus.

Rwindow_set_keyboard_callback.doc: Called when the on-screen keyboard appears, changes height or goes away (mobile). NULL removes it.

Rwindow_clear_focus.doc: No widget of the window has the keyboard focus any more: on mobile, the on-screen keyboard goes away.

Rwindow_set_back_enabled.doc:
R_TRUE while the application has somewhere to go back to (a page
under the one shown). Android 13 and later ask for Back only while the
window wants it (predictive back): at the root page the system handles
Back itself and animates back to the home screen. Default R_FALSE.

Rwindow_wants_back.doc: Returns R_TRUE while Back would be taken: a popup or dialog is open, or Rwindow_set_back_enabled said so.

Rwindow_get_framebuffer_size.doc: Size of the drawable area in pixels.

Rwindow_get_scale.doc: Returns Pixels per logical unit (monitor scale x global UI scale).

Rwindow_focus.doc:
Shows the window in front of the others with the keyboard, and
makes the application the active one. Rwindow_show alone does not take
the keyboard from another application (a prompt that appears while the
user types elsewhere); this is for a window the user just asked for (a
card opened from a tray icon). Where the system has no such request,
the same as Rwindow_show.

Rwindow_is_active.doc: Returns R_TRUE while the window is the one the user is working in.

Rwindow_close.doc:
Asks to close the window, as the close button of its title bar
does: the close callback is asked first and may refuse.

Rwindow_begin_move.doc:
Custom headers. Call these from a mouse-down handler, while the left
button is held: the window follows the pointer until the button is
released (the widget does not receive the release). A
R_WIDGET_HEADER_BAR and the widgets given to Rwidget_set_window_drag do
it by themselves.

Rwindow_set_icon.doc:
Icon of the window (title bar, task bar), from tightly packed
RGBA8 pixels; NULL goes back to the default: on Windows the first icon
of the executable, when it has one. Windows and X11.

Rwindow_set_background.doc:
Image drawn behind the content, scaled to cover the window:
what the glass of a glass theme looks through. R_INVALID_ID removes it.

Rwindow_set_backdrop.doc:
Chooses what shows behind a window created with
R_WINDOW_TRANSPARENT (see RBackdrop). With anything but
R_BACKDROP_NONE the window is not cleared with its color and the
wallpaper of the theme is not drawn: only what the widgets draw hides
the screen. In XML: <Window Backdrop="Blur">.
Returns R_TRUE when the window system does it; R_FALSE (the window
then stays as it was) without R_WINDOW_TRANSPARENT, or when it cannot.

Rwindow_set_theme.doc:
Gives the window a theme of its own, by name ("Dark",
"WindowsLight", or a theme of Rtheme_load): everything inside it (its
content, its island, its menus, lists and dialogs, its background) is
drawn with that theme, while the other windows keep the one of the
application (Rtheme_use). A widget given Rwidget_set_theme keeps its own.
In XML: <Window Theme="...">.
NULL or "": the theme of the application again.
Returns R_FALSE, after reporting an error, when no theme has that name.

Rwindow_get_theme.doc: Returns Name of the theme the window is drawn with (the one of the application when it has none of its own).

Rwindow_has_own_theme.doc: Returns R_TRUE when the window has a theme of its own (Rwindow_set_theme).

Rwindow_set_opacity.doc:
Opacity of the whole window, its frame included, from 0 to 1:
a window that fades, a tool that lets what is under it show.
Returns R_FALSE when the window system cannot do it.

Rwindow_set_topmost.doc:
Keeps the window above the other windows (splash screens, tools).
Returns R_FALSE when the window system cannot do it.

Rwindow_set_owner.doc:
Gives the window an owner (a tool window or an inspector of the
main window): it stays above its owner, has no button of its own in the
taskbar, is minimized and restored with it (where the window system
does it: Windows, X11), and is destroyed with it (everywhere: Raven
destroys the windows a window owns before the window). R_INVALID_ID
gives the window back its independence.
Returns R_FALSE when the window system cannot keep the window with its
owner (it is still destroyed with it), or when the owner is not valid
or is owned by the window (nothing is changed then).

Rwindow_get_owner.doc: Returns The owner of the window (Rwindow_set_owner), or R_INVALID_ID.

Rwindow_set_picture_in_picture.doc:
Picture in picture: the window becomes a small floating window
that stays above the other windows, on every desktop (every space of
macOS, over the applications in full screen too), in a corner of the
work area of its monitor. It loses its title bar where the system
allows: the empty parts of its content move it, its edges resize it,
and its size keeps the proportions it was given. Leaving it gives back
the size, place, frame and state the window had.

Raven does not add a button to leave it: the content shows one, with
the built-in action "window.picture_in_picture" (it goes in and out).
Returns R_FALSE when the window system cannot keep a window above the
others (Wayland): the window is left as it is.

Rwindow_set_picture_in_picture_layout.doc:
Size (logical units) and corner of the window in picture in
picture, for the next time it goes in (now, when it is in). 0, 0 (the
default): 320 wide, with the proportions the content has when it goes
in. The proportions of width / height are kept while the user resizes.

Rwindow_center.doc: Centers the window on the work area of its monitor (no task bar).

Rwindow_set_inspector.doc:
Shows (R_TRUE) or hides (R_FALSE) the inspector of the window: a
window beside it that lists its widgets as a tree, says what the
selected one is (type, name, classes, place and size in the window,
desired size, constraints, slot, visibility, state, style, action,
children) and what the last frame cost (layout, paint and render
times, widgets, instances, draw calls). The selected widget is
outlined in the window, with its type and size. "Pick" selects the
next widget clicked in the window (that click goes to the inspector
only). It follows the window as it changes; closing it hides it, and
it goes with the window. Nothing opens it but this function.

Rwindow_get_inspector.doc: Returns The window of the inspector of a window (to place it), or R_INVALID_ID when it is hidden.

Rwindow_is_splash_screen.doc: Returns R_TRUE for a window created with R_WINDOW_SPLASH_SCREEN (IsSplashScreen in XML).

Rwindow_request_redraw.doc: Asks for a new frame even if no widget changed. Thread-safe.

Rwindow_set_continuous_redraw.doc: R_TRUE redraws the window every frame (games, live viewports).

Rwindow_set_drop_callback.doc:
Takes what is dropped on the window from other applications,
where no widget takes it (Rwidget_set_drop_callback). NULL removes it.

Rdrop_set_highlight_rect.doc:
During R_DROP_ENTER / R_DROP_MOVE only: choose Raven's highlight
in target-local logical units (window-local for a window callback).
Clipped to the target; zero width or height hides it without refusing
the drop. Each callback starts with the default highlight again.
Dimensions must be finite and nonnegative; coordinates must be finite.

Rwindow_get_native_handle.doc: Fills `native` with the OS handles of the window.

Rwindow_capture.doc:
Reads back the last rendered frame as tightly packed RGBA8 pixels.
Blocks until the frame is rendered. Free the result with Rpixels_free.
The alpha is 255, except for a window that is seen through
(R_WINDOW_TRANSPARENT): its pixels are then premultiplied by their
alpha, as the window system receives them.
Returns NULL when the backend cannot capture.

Rwindow_get_focused_widget.doc: Widget that has the keyboard focus in the window, or R_INVALID_ID.

Rwindow_get_hovered_widget.doc: Deepest widget under the cursor, or R_INVALID_ID.

Rwindow_inject_mouse_move.doc:
Inject input as if it came from the OS. Positions are in logical units.
Useful for automated tests, replays and when Raven is driven by a host
application.

Rwindow_inject_composition.doc:
The text an input method is composing (preedit: Chinese,
Japanese, Korean, dead keys), as the platforms send it. The focused
TextInput, SpinBox or TextEditor shows it at its caret, underlined, in
place of its selection, but it is not in its text and no changed
callback runs. [selection_start, selection_end) are bytes of `text`:
the part the input method works on (underlined thicker), or the caret
when they are equal; -1 is the end of `text`. NULL or "" ends the
composition without typing anything (cancel). The committed text comes
through Rwindow_inject_text, which ends the composition too, and so
does a change of focus. Ignored when the focus takes no text.

Rwindow_inject_drag.doc:
A drag from another application moves over the window
(`inside` R_TRUE) or leaves it.
Returns R_TRUE when a drop at this position would be accepted.

Rwindow_inject_drop.doc: Drops files and / or text at a position. Returns R_TRUE when a target took them.

Rwindow_inject_back.doc: Back, as the system sends it (Rwindow_set_back_callback). Returns R_TRUE when something took it.

Rwindow_is_key_down.doc: R_TRUE while the key is held down in the window (cleared when the window loses the keyboard).

Rwindow_is_mouse_button_down.doc: R_TRUE while the mouse button is held down over (or captured by) the window.

Rwindow_get_modifiers.doc: Modifiers (RModifier) of the last input event.

Rwindow_is_mouse_inside.doc: R_TRUE while the pointer is over the client area.

Rwindow_wants_text_input.doc: R_TRUE when the keyboard focus is in a text input, spin box or text editor.

Rwindow_get_text_input_info.doc: The kind of the focused text input; R_FALSE when there is none.

Rwindow_get_text_input_text.doc: Its text (UTF-8), valid until it changes; NULL when there is none.

Rwindow_get_text_input_selection.doc: Its selection: start == end is the caret. R_FALSE when there is none.

Rwindow_set_text_input_selection.doc: Selects bytes [start, end) of it (end before start puts the caret at end).

Rwindow_replace_text_input.doc:
Replaces bytes [start, end) of it with `text` and puts the caret
after it, as typing would (the changed callback runs; MaxLength
applies). R_FALSE when there is none or it is read-only.

Rwindow_get_text_composition.doc:
The composition of the input method in progress (UTF-8, valid
until it changes) and its selection in bytes; NULL when there is none.
Any output pointer may be NULL.

Rwindow_has_popup.doc: R_TRUE while a menu, list or dialog is open over the window.

Rwindow_get_text_input_rect.doc:
Last painted caret in window pixels (x, y, width, height), including scrolling and scale.
Call after Rdraw_frame. Independent of the blink phase. Returns R_FALSE and zeros the
outputs when there is no visible editable caret, the window is inactive, or focus changed
since painting. Any output pointer may be NULL. While an input method
composes, it is the caret inside the composition: where its candidate
window goes.

Rwindow_get_popup_count.doc: Returns Number of open in-window popups (menus, combo lists, pickers), bottom to top.

Rwindow_get_popup.doc: Returns Root widget of popup `index`, whose rect is in window coordinates; R_INVALID_ID out of range.

Rwindow_set_tab_navigation.doc: R_FALSE: Tab no longer moves the keyboard focus (the application uses it as a shortcut). Default R_TRUE.

Rdrag_begin.doc:
Starts dragging `data` from `source` (call it while a mouse button
is held, typically from a mouse-move event once the pointer has moved
a few units). Until the button is released, the widgets with a drop
callback (Rwidget_set_drop_callback) under the pointer receive
R_DROP_ENTER / MOVE / LEAVE and, on release, R_DROP_DROPPED, with
`drag_type` set and `text` = `data`. Returning R_FALSE from the callback
refuses the drop there. Escape cancels. `label` follows the pointer.
Returns R_FALSE when the widget is not in a window.

Rdrag_is_active.doc: R_TRUE while a drag started by Rdrag_begin is in progress in the window.

Rdrag_get_type.doc: Type of the drag in progress, or NULL.

Rdrag_get_data.doc: Data of the drag in progress, or NULL.

Rdrag_cancel.doc: Ends the drag in progress without dropping (the target receives R_DROP_LEAVE).

Rtouch_get_settings.doc: The settings every window follows, unless it has its own.

Rtouch_set_settings.doc: Changes them; NULL puts back the defaults.

Rwindow_set_touch_settings.doc: Settings of one window; NULL: it follows Rtouch_set_settings again.

Rwindow_get_touch_settings.doc: The settings the window follows (its own, or those of the application).

Rwidget_set_touch_mode.doc: What a finger does on the widget and what it contains (default R_TOUCH_MODE_AUTO: as its parent says).

Rwidget_set_touch_gestures.doc: R_FALSE: two fingers (on the screen or a trackpad) neither zoom nor pan the widget (default R_TRUE).

Rwidget_set_pen_mouse.doc: R_FALSE: the pen is not a mouse on the widget and what it contains; only its pen callback sees it (default R_TRUE).

Rwindow_is_pen_in_range.doc: R_TRUE while a pen is near the screen over the window.

Rwindow_is_touch_active.doc: R_TRUE when the pointer last used in the window was a finger (the interface may then be made larger).

Rwindow_inject_touch.doc: A finger: R_TOUCH_DOWN, then R_TOUCH_MOVE..., then R_TOUCH_UP, with the same `id`.

Rwindow_inject_pen.doc: A pen: `pressure` 0..1 as the pen would give it, `buttons` a bitmask of RPenButton.

Rwindow_inject_trackpad_gesture.doc:
A gesture of a trackpad, as the system recognizes it: R_GESTURE_BEGIN,
R_GESTURE_UPDATE..., then R_GESTURE_END. (x, y) is the pointer, `scale_delta`
and `rotation_delta` (degrees, clockwise) what changed since the previous
event, `pan_x`, `pan_y` how far the fingers moved since then.

Rwindow_inject_trackpad_scroll.doc:
Two fingers scrolling on a trackpad: (dx, dy) is how far they moved
(logical units), the content following them. Sent as a precise wheel
(REvent::wheel_precise) at the pointer.

Rwindow_inject_trackpad_scroll_end.doc:
The fingers that scrolled left the trackpad, on a system that
leaves the inertia to the application (Wayland): flicked content keeps
going (Touch.Inertia).

Rwindow_advance_touch.doc:
Advances the inertia of flicked content by `seconds` at once,
and fires a long press that is due, without waiting (tests).

Rlook_set.doc:
Changes the look of the application. The theme file in use, if
it names no look of its own, is laid again over the new one; colors
and metrics changed with Rtheme_set_... are lost; what was given to
widgets (Rwidget_set_color...) is kept.

Rlook_set(R_LOOK_NATIVE_LIGHT);   the look of the platform, light

Theme files that name no look (no Look attribute) follow it too, so a
part of a window given one (Theme="paper.xml") changes with it.

Rlook_get.doc: The look given to Rlook_set (R_LOOK_RAVEN_DARK at start).

Rtheme_apply.doc: deprecated Rlook_set: a built-in theme is a look of Raven.

Rtheme_set_metric.doc:
Changes a size of the theme in use. It lasts until the look or
the theme is chosen again (Rlook_set, Rtheme_use), but not through a
switch between light and dark made by Rtheme_follow_system.

Rtheme_set_material.doc:
Material of every widget that was not given one with
Rwidget_set_material. Rtheme_apply sets it: solid for the flat
themes, frosted glass for the glass themes.

Rtheme_set_font.doc: Font used by widgets that have no font of their own.

Rtheme_set_accent.doc:
Sets the accent color and everything that follows from it: its
hovered and pressed shades, the focus outline, the selection, the links.

Rtheme_set_dark.doc:
Tells whether the theme is a dark one. It decides the tint of
the glass, the colors of the code and which wallpaper the glass themes
use. Rtheme_apply and the theme files set it.

Rtheme_get_system_dark.doc: R_TRUE when the system is in dark mode, R_FALSE in light mode, -1 when the platform does not tell (desktop today).

Rtheme_follow_system.doc:
Follows the dark or light mode of the system with the Raven look
(R_LOOK_RAVEN_DARK / R_LOOK_RAVEN_LIGHT), now and when it changes.
Off by default. Does nothing where the platform does not tell (desktop today).

A switch is Rlook_set, except that the sizes given with
Rtheme_set_metric stay. Colors and styles set with Rtheme_set_... are
those of one mode and are lost; to keep colors, sizes and styles of
the application through the switch, put them in a theme that names no
look (Rtheme_load_from_memory, then Rtheme_use): it is laid over the
new look.

Rtheme_set_wallpaper.doc:
Image drawn behind the content of the windows that have no
background of their own, or R_INVALID_ID for none (the window color).

Rtheme_set_style_color.doc:
Gives a color to the widgets of a type and / or of a class,
instead of the color of the theme.
Tag of a type of widget ("Button"), or NULL for every type.
A class (Rwidget_set_class, Class="..."), or NULL
for the widgets of the type whatever their classes.

When several styles give the same value to a widget, the one with a
type and a class wins over the one with a class, which wins over the
one with a type; between equals, the last one set wins.

Rtheme_set_style_material.doc: R_MATERIAL_DEFAULT removes the material of the style.

Rtheme_clear_styles.doc: Removes every style of the theme. Rtheme_apply and Rtheme_use do it too.

Rtheme_load.doc:
Reads a theme file and keeps the theme under its name (the Name
attribute, else the name of the file). It does not change the theme in
use unless a theme of that name is the one in use.

The file is watched like the interface files (Rxml_set_live_reload):
saving it updates every widget that uses the theme.
Returns The name of the theme, valid until Rshutdown, or NULL after
reporting an error.

Rtheme_load_from_memory.doc: Same, from a text. `size` may be 0 for a null-terminated text.

Rtheme_use.doc:
Makes a named theme the theme of the application: a theme
given by Rtheme_load (laid over the look in use when it names no
look), or the name of a look ("WindowsLight", "RavenDark"; the old
"Dark", "Light", "GlassDark"... too), which is then Rlook_set.
Values changed with Rtheme_set_... are lost.
Returns R_FALSE, after reporting an error, when no theme has that name.

Rtheme_get_name.doc: Name of the theme in use ("Dark" at start).

Rtheme_get_count.doc: Number of named themes, the four built-in ones included.

Rtheme_get_name_at.doc: Name of the index-th one, or NULL.

Rtheme_save.doc:
Writes the theme in use, with every change made since it was
applied, as a theme file.
Name given to the theme in the file; NULL keeps the current one.

Rfont_create.doc:
Creates a font from the content of a .ttf / .otf file.
The buffer is copied. Glyphs are rasterized on demand, at the exact
pixel size needed by each window scale, into a shared atlas.
Returns R_INVALID_ID on failure.

Rfont_get_default.doc: Returns The font embedded in the library (Roboto, Latin and Latin Extended-A).

Rfont_get_monospace.doc:
Returns The fixed-width font embedded in the library (Roboto Mono, same
characters), used by default by the text editors. In XML: Font="monospace".

Rfont_set_fallback.doc:
Font used for the characters missing from `font` (symbols, icons,
other scripts). Fallbacks can be chained.

Rfont_set_variant.doc:
Gives a font the font to use for one of its styles: the bold
file of the same family, its italic file. Formatted text (Markdown
labels, the Markdown of the text editor) uses them.

A font that was given none still has the three styles: Raven draws
its glyphs thicker for bold and slanted for italic, keeping their
advances, so that text does not move when its style changes.
R_INVALID_ID goes back to the style Raven derives.

Rfont_get_variant.doc:
Returns The font drawn for a style of `font`: the one given with
Rfont_set_variant, else the one Raven derives from it (made on first
use; it lives as long as `font` and cannot be deleted by itself).
Usable wherever a font is: Rlabel_set_font, Rdraw_text...

Rfont_measure_text.doc:
Measures a UTF-8 string, in logical units, at scale 1.
R_INVALID_ID uses the theme font.
Font size; 0 uses R_METRIC_FONT_SIZE.

Rtexture_create.doc:
Creates a texture from the content of an image file (PNG, JPEG,
BMP, TGA, GIF, PSD, SVG). Decoding happens on the calling thread.
Returns R_INVALID_ID on failure.

Rtexture_create_async.doc:
Same as Rtexture_create, decoded on a worker thread. The handle
is usable at once; widgets showing it draw nothing until it is ready.
The buffer is copied.

Rtexture_create_from_svg.doc:
Draws an SVG image (an icon) into a texture, at `scale` pixels per
unit of the SVG. The widgets show it at the size the SVG gives, whatever
the scale (Rtexture_get_density).

0 or less: at the size it is shown. It is first drawn at a scale of 2;
once painted, it is drawn again (on a worker thread) with as many pixels
as the screen shows it with: the scale of the monitor of the window, an
Image that stretches it, a zoom. It follows when the window moves to a
screen of another density or the image grows, and comes down when it is
shown much smaller (sides of at most 4096 pixels). Its width and height
in pixels (Rtexture_get_size) change then; its size in logical units
does not. Rtexture_create, Rtexture_create_from_file and the asynchronous
ones read SVG files this way. Paths, fills, strokes and gradients are
drawn; text, filters and masks are not.

Rtexture_get_density.doc: Pixels of the texture per logical unit: the scale of an SVG, 1 otherwise.

Rtexture_create_from_file_async.doc: Reads and decodes the file on a worker thread.

Rtexture_create_from_pixels.doc: Creates a texture from tightly packed RGBA8 pixels (straight alpha). Its filter is R_FILTER_LINEAR.

Rtexture_update.doc:
Replaces the pixels of a texture. The size may change. Use it to
show frames produced on the CPU or read back from another renderer.

Rimage_decode.doc:
Decodes an image file held in memory (PNG, JPEG, BMP, TGA) into
tightly packed RGBA8 pixels, without making a texture: for pictures
that arrive one after the other and go to Rtexture_update. Thread-safe,
so that the decoding can be done away from the UI thread.
Returns The pixels, to release with Rpixels_free; NULL when the data
is not an image Raven can read.

Rpixels_free.doc: Releases pixels returned by Raven (Rimage_decode, Rwindow_capture). Thread-safe.

Rimage_encode_png.doc:
Encodes tightly packed RGBA8 pixels (what Rwindow_capture
returns) as a PNG file in memory. Thread-safe.
Receives the number of bytes.
Returns The bytes of the file, to release with Rpixels_free; NULL when
there are no pixels.

Rimage_save_png.doc:
Writes tightly packed RGBA8 pixels to a PNG file: a screenshot
of Rwindow_capture, a picture made by the application. Thread-safe.
Returns R_FALSE when the file cannot be written.

Rtexture_is_ready.doc: Returns R_TRUE once an asynchronous texture is decoded (or failed).

Rtexture_wait.doc: Blocks until an asynchronous texture is ready.

Rtexture_set_filter.doc:
How the texture is smoothed when it is scaled. The textures made
from image files start with R_FILTER_MIPMAP, the others with
R_FILTER_LINEAR.

Rwidget_create.doc:
Creates a widget. It is not shown until it is added to a parent
that belongs to a window (Rwidget_add_child, Rwindow_set_content).

Rwidget_destroy.doc: Deletes a widget and all its descendants.

Rwidget_add_child.doc:
Appends a child to a panel. The parent takes ownership.
A widget that already has a parent is moved.
Returns `child`, so calls can be nested:
Rid ok = Rwidget_add_child(row, Rbutton_create("OK"));
R_INVALID_ID when the child replaced in a single-child container
had a destroy callback that destroyed the container or `child`;
`child`, when it is still there, is then not added.

Rwidget_remove_child.doc: Detaches a child without deleting it. The caller owns it again.

Rwidget_clear_children.doc: Deletes every child of a panel.

Rwidget_get_window.doc: Returns The window showing the widget, or R_INVALID_ID.

Rwidget_find.doc:
Finds a widget by name.
A window or a widget; the search covers its whole subtree.
Returns R_INVALID_ID when no widget has that name.

Rslot_set_padding.doc: Space kept around the child, inside its slot. All panels.

Rslot_set_halign.doc: Alignment of the child inside its slot. Default: fill. All panels.

Rslot_set_auto.doc:
The slot takes the desired size of the child along the panel
direction (Slate AutoWidth / AutoHeight). This is the default.
VBox, HBox.

Rslot_set_fill.doc:
The slot shares the space left by the auto slots, in proportion
to `coefficient` (Slate FillWidth / FillHeight). VBox, HBox.
In a Splitter, the coefficient is the relative size of the pane.

Rslot_set_max_size.doc: Upper bound of the slot along the panel direction. 0 = none. VBox, HBox.

Rslot_set_grid.doc: Cell of the child. Grid, UniformGrid.

Rslot_set_anchors.doc:
Canvas placement. Anchors are fractions of the canvas size (0..1).
- anchors equal on an axis: the child is at anchor + position, with
the slot size (or its desired size when the slot size is <= 0);
- anchors different on an axis: the child stretches between them,
position and size are then the near and far margins.
Alignment is the pivot of the child (0,0 = top-left, 0.5,0.5 = center).

Rslot_set_title.doc: Title of the tab showing the child. TabView.

Rwidget_set_enabled.doc: A disabled widget ignores input and is drawn dimmed, with its descendants.

Rwidget_set_hit_testable.doc: R_FALSE lets mouse events pass through the widget (not its children).

Rwidget_set_opacity.doc: Opacity multiplier applied to the widget and its descendants (0..1).

Rwidget_set_transition.doc:
Gives the widget a transition that plays each time it appears:
when its window is first drawn, when it is added to a window that is
shown, and when it becomes visible again (Rwidget_set_visibility, a
tab or a switcher showing it). In XML: Appear="FlyUp" AppearDelay="0.1".
Time before it starts. Give growing delays to the
items of a group to make them arrive one after the other.

Rwidget_play_transition.doc: Plays a transition once, now, whatever the widget was given with Rwidget_set_transition.

Rwidget_set_clipping.doc: R_TRUE clips the descendants to the bounds of the widget.

Rwidget_set_tooltip.doc:
Text shown when the cursor rests on the widget. NULL removes it. A label, which otherwise
lets the mouse through, takes the hover while it has a tooltip (events it does not use still bubble).

Rwidget_get_tooltip.doc: Returns The tooltip text of the widget, "" when it has none.

Rwidget_set_size.doc:
Size constraints, in logical units. They apply to the desired size the
widget reports to its parent. A negative value removes the constraint
on that axis.

Rwidget_get_rect.doc: Bounds of the widget in its window, in logical units, after the last layout.

Rwidget_focus.doc: Gives the keyboard focus to the widget, and scrolls it into view (Rwidget_scroll_into_view).

Rwidget_set_action.doc:
Name of the action fired by the main event of the widget: button
click, value change, text commit, item activation (see Raction_bind).

Rwidget_set_drop_callback.doc:
Makes the widget a target for what is dragged from other
applications: files from the file manager, text. It is highlighted
while a drop on it would be accepted. NULL removes the callback.

Rwidget_set_window_drag.doc:
In a window created with R_WINDOW_CUSTOM_HEADER: dragging the
widget moves the window and a double click maximizes it, as a title bar
does. The buttons, fields and other controls inside it keep working.
In XML: WindowDrag="true".

Rwidget_hit_test.doc: Deepest widget of a subtree under a point of its window, or R_INVALID_ID.

Rwidget_pick.doc:
Deepest visible widget of a subtree under a point of its window,
whether it reacts to the pointer or not: a label, a panel, a disabled
button. What a design tool selects with a click.

Rwidget_set_context_menu.doc: Menu opened by a right click on the widget. The widget does not own it.

Rwidget_invalidate.doc: Asks for the widget to be laid out and painted again.

Rwidget_set_color.doc:
Overrides a theme color for one widget. R_COLOR_TEXT is also
inherited by its descendants.

Rwidget_get_color.doc:
The color the widget is drawn with for a role: its own, else
the one of the styles of its theme that apply to it, else the one of
its theme. What a custom widget should draw itself with.

Rwidget_set_material.doc:
Gives one widget a material of its own, whatever the theme:
a solid button in a glass window, a panel of clear glass in a flat one.
A widget that draws no surface (a box, a label) gets one of this
material behind it: any widget can become a panel of glass.
In XML: Material="Glass | FrostedGlass | TintedGlass | Solid".
R_MATERIAL_DEFAULT follows the theme again.

Rwidget_get_material.doc: Returns The material the widget is drawn with: its own, or the one of the theme.

Rwidget_set_metric.doc: Overrides a theme metric for one widget.

Rwidget_get_metric.doc:
Returns The metric the widget uses: its own, else the one of a style,
else the one of its theme; grown for larger text
(Raccessibility_set_text_scale) and for a finger (RTouchSettings::min_touch_size).

Rwidget_set_class.doc:
Classes of the widget, separated by spaces ("danger large"):
the styles of the theme made for these classes apply to it
(Rtheme_set_style_color, <Style Class="danger" .../> in a theme file).
In XML: Class="...". NULL or "" removes them.

Rwidget_get_class.doc: Returns The classes, "" when it has none. Valid until they change.

Rwidget_set_theme.doc:
Gives the widget and everything inside it a theme of their own,
by name ("Dark", "GlassLight", or a theme of Rtheme_load): a dark side
bar in a light window, a preview of another theme. Menus and lists
opened from inside follow. In XML: Theme="...".
NULL or "" follows the parent (the application theme) again.
Returns R_FALSE, after reporting an error, when no theme has that name.

Rwidget_get_theme.doc: Returns Name of the theme the widget is drawn with.

Rwidget_set_font.doc:
Gives the widget and everything inside it a font, for the texts
that have none of their own (a label given Rlabel_set_font keeps its
own): a tool whose panels wear one font while the interface it shows
keeps the font of the application. Menus and lists opened from inside
follow.
R_INVALID_ID: the font of the parent (in the end, the one of the theme, Rtheme_set_font) again.

Rwidget_get_font.doc: Returns The font given to the widget itself, or R_INVALID_ID.

Rgrid_set_column_fill.doc:
Lets a column / row grow to take a share of the free space
(Slate FillColumn / FillRow). 0 sizes it to its content (default).

Runiform_grid_set_columns.doc:
Places children automatically, left to right then top to bottom,
in the given number of columns. 0 uses the grid cell of each slot (default).

Rborder_set_padding.doc: Space between the outline and the child.

Rborder_set_background.doc: Background color (R_COLOR_PANEL of this widget). Alpha 0 draws no background.

Rborder_set_outline.doc: Outline width and color. Width 0 draws no outline (default).

Rborder_set_shadow.doc: Soft drop shadow behind the border. Blur 0 disables it (default).

Rborder_set_material.doc:
What the border is made of. R_MATERIAL_GLASS turns it into a
panel of glass tinted by its background color (the alpha of the color
is the strength of the tint): floating tool bars, side bars, cards.

Rsize_box_set_aspect_ratio.doc:
Keeps the child at a fixed width / height ratio, as large as fits.
0 disables it (default). The fixed, minimum and maximum sizes are set
with Rwidget_set_size, Rwidget_set_min_size and Rwidget_set_max_size.

Rscroll_box_set_orientation.doc: Direction in which children are stacked and scrolled. Default: R_VERTICAL.

Rscroll_box_set_scroll_both.doc: R_TRUE also scrolls across the stacking direction when the content is too large.

Rwidget_scroll_into_view.doc:
Scrolls every ScrollBox above the widget so that the widget is
visible. The library does it by itself for the focused widget when the
focus comes from Tab or Rwidget_focus, and for a text field above the
on-screen keyboard (Rwindow_get_keyboard_area).

Rsplitter_set_orientation.doc: R_HORIZONTAL puts the panes side by side (default), R_VERTICAL stacks them.

Rbackground_blur_create.doc:
Creates a panel that shows what is behind it out of focus,
with one child over it. In XML:

<BackgroundBlur Style="Frosted" Radius="24" CornerRadius="18" Padding="16">
<Label>Over a blurred view of the window</Label>
</BackgroundBlur>

It works in any theme and with any material: it is not the glass of
the glass themes (which bends and reflects), but the looks of
RBlurStyle. Unlike the opacity of a widget, it does not let what is
behind show sharp.

Rbackground_blur_set_radius.doc:
How far what is behind goes out of focus, in logical units:
4 softens, 20 hides the details, 60 leaves only colors. A negative
value (the default) uses R_METRIC_BLUR_RADIUS of the theme.

Rbackground_blur_set_tint.doc:
Color laid over the blur; its alpha is how much of it. Without
one, R_BLUR_PLAIN has none and the other styles take theirs from the
theme (R_COLOR_PANEL).

Rbackground_blur_clear_tint.doc: Removes the tint given with Rbackground_blur_set_tint.

Rbackground_blur_set_saturation.doc: Saturation of what is seen through: 1 = as it is, 0 = gray, 1.5 = vivid. Negative = the one of the style.

Rbackground_blur_set_grain.doc: Fine grain over the blur, 0 = none .. 1. Negative = the one of the style.

Rbackground_blur_set_padding.doc: Space between the edge and the child.

Rbackground_blur_set_shadow.doc: Soft shadow under the panel; blur 0 = none (default).

Rtab_view_add_tab.doc:
Adds a page. Same as Rwidget_add_child followed by Rslot_set_title.
Returns The index of the new tab, or -1.

Rtab_view_set_documents.doc:
Documents mode: the major tabs of an application (the level,
then one tab per open asset, as in Unreal): tabs on the left with an
icon and a close button (a middle click closes too), shrinking when
they do not fit, no slide between pages. XML: Documents="true".

Rtab_view_get_tab.doc: The page of a tab, R_INVALID_ID if none.

Rtab_view_find_tab.doc: Index of the tab of a page, -1 if none.

Rtab_view_set_tab_icon.doc: Icon before the title (documents). R_INVALID_ID removes it; tint: a mask in the text color.

Rtab_view_set_tab_closable.doc: R_FALSE: no close button (documents ; the level tab). Tabs can be closed by default.

Rtab_view_show_tab.doc: Shows the tab of a page (the changed callback is called).

Rset_layout_direction.doc: Direction of every window: R_DIRECTION_AUTO (the default), _LTR or _RTL.

Rget_layout_direction.doc: The direction the windows use now: R_DIRECTION_LTR or _RTL.

Rwidget_set_direction.doc: Direction of a part of a window: R_DIRECTION_INHERIT, _LTR or _RTL.

Rwidget_get_direction.doc: The direction the widget is laid out in: R_DIRECTION_LTR or _RTL.

Rlabel_set_text.doc: Sets the text. '\n' starts a new line.

Rlabel_set_text_size.doc: Font size in logical units. 0 uses R_METRIC_FONT_SIZE.

Rlabel_set_wrap.doc: R_TRUE wraps the text on the width given by the parent.

Rlabel_set_markdown.doc:
R_TRUE reads the text as Markdown and shows it formatted
(Markdown="true" in XML):

# titles, **strong**, *emphasis*, `code`, ~~struck~~, [links](url),
lists and lists in lists, - [x] task lists, > quotes, --- rules,
| tables |, images alone on their line, and ``` blocks of code with
the colors of their language (```c, ```python...: the languages of
the text editor, raven_text_editor.h).

The text wraps on the width of the label unless Rlabel_set_wrap said
otherwise; put the label in a scroll box for a long document. Strong
and emphasized text use the bold and italic of the font
(Rfont_set_variant), which Raven derives from the font itself when it
was given none. The colors come from the theme: R_COLOR_LINK,
R_COLOR_CODE, R_COLOR_SEPARATOR, R_COLOR_ACCENT.

Rlabel_get_plain_text.doc: The text of a Markdown label without its marks, as a reader sees it. Valid until the next call.

Rlabel_set_selectable.doc:
R_TRUE lets the user select the text of the label with the
mouse, as on a web page (Selectable="true" in XML): drag to select, a
double click selects a word, a triple click a paragraph, Shift + click
extends the selection; then Ctrl+C (Cmd+C) copies it and Ctrl+A selects
everything. A click elsewhere takes the selection away. Plain and
Markdown labels alike: a copy of a Markdown label is its text without
the marks, and its links are still clicked, not selected. The label
takes the mouse (what holds it no longer receives the clicks on it) and
the keyboard after a click; Tab passes it by. Default R_FALSE.

Rlabel_get_selected_text.doc: The text selected, as Ctrl+C copies it ("" when nothing is). Valid until the next call.

Rlabel_select_all.doc: Selects the whole text of a selectable label.

Rbutton_set_text.doc:
Sets the content of the button to a label. A button can instead
hold any single child widget (Rwidget_add_child), e.g. an HBox with an icon.

Rslider_get_range.doc: The range given with Rslider_set_range and the step (NULL for what is not wanted).

Rslider_set_step.doc: Snaps the value to multiples of `step`. 0 = continuous (default).

Rimage_set_tint_text.doc: R_TRUE: the image is tinted with the text color around it (white icons that follow the theme). XML: TintText.

Rimage_set_region.doc: Part of the texture to show, in UV coordinates. Default: 0, 0, 1, 1.

Rtext_input_set_placeholder.doc: Dimmed text shown while the input is empty.

Rtext_input_set_max_length.doc: Maximum number of characters. 0 = no limit (default).

Rtext_input_set_input_type.doc: What it holds: picks the on-screen keyboard on mobile. Default: R_TEXT_INPUT_TYPE_TEXT.

Rtext_input_set_return_key.doc: The return key of the on-screen keyboard (Done, Next, Search...). Default: R_RETURN_KEY_DEFAULT.

Rtext_input_set_committed_callback.doc: Called when Enter is pressed. This also fires the action of the widget.

Rspin_box_get_range.doc: The range and the step (NULL for what is not wanted).

Rspin_box_set_decimals.doc: Digits shown after the decimal point. Default: 2.

Rspin_box_set_buttons.doc:
Step buttons in the looks of Raven too: a down button at the left
end and an up button at the right end, the value between them (XML
`Buttons="True"`). A click steps once; holding a button repeats its step.
The platform looks (Windows, GNOME, macOS) always draw their own buttons.
Default: R_FALSE (drag to scrub, arrows / wheel to step).

Rcombo_box_add_item.doc: Returns The index of the new item.

Rlist_view_add_item.doc: Returns The index of the new item.

Rlist_view_set_activated_callback.doc: Called on double click or Enter. This also fires the action of the widget.

Rtree_view_add_item.doc:
Adds an item.
Item to add under, or R_INVALID_ID for a top-level item.
Returns The handle of the new item.

Rtree_item_destroy.doc: Deletes an item and its descendants.

Rtree_item_get_parent.doc: Returns The parent item, or R_INVALID_ID for a top-level item.

Rtree_view_set_selected_item.doc: Selects an item. R_INVALID_ID selects nothing.

Rtree_view_set_activated_callback.doc: Called on double click or Enter. This also fires the action of the widget.

Rtree_item_set_icon.doc: Icon drawn before the text of the item (a region u0,v0,u1,v1 of the texture). R_INVALID_ID removes it.

Rtree_item_set_text_color.doc: Color of the text of the item; alpha 0 goes back to the theme.

Rtree_view_set_multi_select.doc:
Several items can be selected: Ctrl + click adds or removes one,
Shift + click selects a range. The selection callback receives the item
clicked last (the primary one, Rtree_view_get_selected_item).

Rtree_view_set_drag_type.doc:
Items can be dragged: the selection is given to Rdrag_begin with
this type and, as data, the handles of the items in decimal separated
by spaces. NULL: no drag (default).

Rtree_view_get_item_at.doc: Item at a point relative to the tree (drop callbacks give local_x, local_y), or R_INVALID_ID.

Rtree_view_set_drop_highlight.doc: Highlights where a drop would go: an item, or the whole tree (`whole_tree`). R_INVALID_ID, 0 removes it.

Rmenu_bar_set_native.doc:
The menu bar of the system. On macOS, the first MenuBar of a
window is shown in the bar at the top of the screen while the window is
the active one, after the menu of the application (About, Hide, Quit);
it then takes no room in the window. Its shortcuts are those of the
system: R_MOD_SUPER is Command, R_MOD_CTRL is Control. Elsewhere it is
drawn in the window. On by default; R_FALSE keeps it in the window
everywhere. In XML: <MenuBar Native="false">.

Rmenu_bar_is_native.doc: Returns R_TRUE while the menu bar is shown by the system instead of the window.

Rmenu_add_menu.doc: Creates a menu inside a menu bar or as a sub-menu of another menu.

Rmenu_add_header.doc: A noninteractive caption row, skipped by keyboard navigation.

Rmenu_bar_add_divider.doc: A vertical divider between titles of an in-window MenuBar. Ignored by native macOS bars.

Rmenu_set_title_color.doc: Title color in an in-window bar; alpha 0 restores the theme. Ignored by native macOS bars.

Rmenu_item_set_shortcut.doc:
Shows a shortcut next to the item and triggers the item when the
keys are pressed in the window of its menu bar.

Rmenu_item_set_shortcut_text.doc:
Display-only shortcut hint; copied, never binds a key. Overrides
the formatted shortcut without changing its binding. NULL restores the
formatted shortcut; an empty string hides it. XML: ShortcutText.

Rmenu_item_set_icon.doc:
Icon drawn before the text of a menu item (after the check mark column).
R_INVALID_ID removes it. u0, v0, u1, v1 : region of the texture.
R_TRUE: the texture is a mask drawn in the text color (monochrome icons).

Rmenu_open.doc: Opens a menu as a popup at a position of the window (logical units).

Rwindow_close_popups.doc: Closes every open menu and popup of the window.

Rtile_view_set_items.doc: Gives the tiles: `count` of them, described by `callback`. The selection is cleared.

Rtile_view_refresh.doc: Draws the tiles again (their description changed, not their number).

Rtile_view_set_tile_size.doc: Size of a tile (its name included) and of its icon. Default 112 x 112, icon 64.

Rtile_view_set_icon_width.doc:
Layout="Rows": width of the box the icon is drawn in (its height is the
icon size), for icons that are not square; 0 = square (default). XML: IconWidth.

Rtile_view_set_sections.doc: `count` sections, described by `callback`, all unfolded. Rtile_view_set_items removes them: give them after the tiles.

Rtile_view_get_section_of.doc: The section of a tile, or -1 (before the first section).

Rtile_view_set_section_folded.doc: Folds or unfolds a section (the toggled callback is not called).

Rtile_view_get_section_at.doc: The section whose header is at a point relative to the widget, or -1.

Rtile_view_set_section_toggled_callback.doc: Called when the user folds or unfolds a section (`index`: the section).

Rtile_view_get_selection.doc: Index of the nth selected tile, in order.

Rtile_view_get_item_at.doc: Tile at a point relative to the widget (drop callbacks give local_x, local_y), or -1.

Rtile_view_set_drop_highlight.doc: Highlights the tile a drop would go to; -1 removes it.

Rtile_view_set_drag_type.doc:
Tiles can be dragged: the selected tiles are given to Rdrag_begin
with this type and, as data, their indices separated by spaces.

Rtable_add_column.doc:
Adds a column.
Width in logical units; 0 or less gives the default (120).
Returns The index of the column. The stored rows get an empty cell in it.

Rtable_clear_columns.doc: Removes the columns and the stored rows.

Rtable_get_column_width.doc: The width the column has on screen (a filling column takes more than its width).

Rtable_set_column_fill.doc: > 0: the column takes this share of the room the others leave; 0: its width only.

Rtable_set_column_sortable.doc: R_FALSE: a click on the header does not sort (default R_TRUE).

Rtable_set_column_align.doc: Where the texts sit in the cells: 0 left, 0.5 center, 1 right.

Rtable_add_row.doc:
Adds a row.
The texts of the cells, separated by '|' ("Ada|36|London"),
or NULL for an empty row; Rtable_set_cell gives a text holding a '|'.
Returns The index of the row.

Rtable_set_cell_text_color.doc:
Stored rows: a fixed text color; column -1 colors the row; cells override it.
Alpha 0 restores the inherited/theme color. A color from the cell color callback wins over it.

Rtable_set_multi_select.doc: Opt into Ctrl/Cmd toggles and Shift ranges; single selection is the default.

Rtable_get_selection.doc: Selected row at index, top to bottom; -1 outside the selection.

Rtable_set_selected.doc: Replaces the selection with one row. -1 selects nothing, including in multi-select mode.

Rtable_sort.doc: Sorts by a column (stored rows are moved); -1 shows no sorted column.

Rtable_set_striped.doc: Every other row a little darker.

Rtable_set_activated_callback.doc: Called on double click or Enter. This also fires the action of the widget.

Rdate_picker_set_date.doc: Sets the date (today when the picker is created). An invalid date is refused.

Rdate_picker_set_range.doc: The earliest and the latest dates that can be chosen; 0 for year leaves that side open.

Rdate_picker_set_format.doc:
How the field writes the date: YYYY, MM, M, DD, D, MMMM (the name
of the month), MMM (its first three letters), dddd (the name of the day),
ddd; anything else is kept. Default "YYYY-MM-DD"; "D MMMM YYYY" gives "3 November 2026".

Rdate_picker_get_text.doc: The date as the field shows it (valid until the next call).

Rtime_picker_set_minute_step.doc: Step of the minutes for the arrows and the wheel (default 1).

Rtoast_show.doc: Shows a message for `seconds` (0 or less: until Rtoast_hide), with the kind and button set now.

Rtoast_show_kind.doc: Same, with a kind of its own (the kind set by Rtoast_set_kind is left as it is).

Rtoast_hide.doc: Hides the newest message shown; the next one waiting comes.

Rtoast_clear.doc: Hides every message, and forgets those waiting.

Rtoast_get_count.doc: Returns The messages shown and waiting.

Rtoast_get_text.doc: Returns The newest message shown (the last one, once hidden; the clicked one in the action callback).

Rtoast_set_max_visible.doc: How many messages a R_TOAST_STACK shows at once (default 3).

Rtoast_set_kind.doc: The kind of the next messages (and of the message shown, with R_TOAST_REPLACE).

Rtoast_set_action_text.doc: A button at the end of the next messages ("Undo"); NULL or "" removes it.

Rbreadcrumb_set_items.doc: Replaces the items: their texts separated by '|'.

Rbreadcrumb_add_item.doc: Returns The index of the new item, at the end.

Rbreadcrumb_truncate.doc: Keeps the first `count` items: Rbreadcrumb_truncate(b, index + 1) goes back to the item clicked.

Rrating_set_value.doc: The score, from 0 to the number of stars.

Rrating_set_allow_half.doc: Half stars can be chosen (a whole star by default).

Rrating_set_read_only.doc: Shown only, the user cannot change it.

Rpagination_set_siblings.doc: Page numbers shown around the current one (default 1).

Rplot_add_series.doc: Adds a series (its name in the legend; NULL or "": not in the legend). Returns its index.

Rplot_clear.doc: Removes every series and every drag line.

Rplot_set_series_data.doc:
Replaces the points of a series with `count` points, copied.
The X of the points, or NULL: 0, 1, 2...
The Y of the points. NaN leaves a gap in the line.

Rplot_append_series_data.doc: Adds points after those of a series (x NULL: numbered after the last one).

Rplot_add_point.doc: Adds one point after those of a series.

Rplot_get_point.doc: One point of a series. Returns R_FALSE when there is no such point.

Rplot_set_series_max_points.doc: Keeps only the last `max` points of a series, for data that streams in (0: all of them, the default).

Rplot_set_series_color.doc: The color of a series (by default the next one of a palette of ten).

Rplot_set_series_line.doc: How the line is drawn and how wide (default solid, 1.75; width 0 keeps the width).

Rplot_set_series_marker.doc: The mark on each point and its radius (default none, 4; size 0 keeps the size).

Rplot_set_series_marker_filled.doc: Filled markers (the default) or only their outline.

Rplot_set_series_step.doc: Draws the line in steps: along at the height of a point, then up or down to the next.

Rplot_set_series_fill.doc: Shades the area between the line and zero, at this opacity (0: none, the default).

Rplot_set_series_axes.doc: The axes a series is drawn against: R_PLOT_X or R_PLOT_X2, R_PLOT_Y or R_PLOT_Y2.

Rplot_set_series_visible.doc: Shows or hides a series (the user does it with a click on its name in the legend).

Rplot_set_axis_label.doc: The name written along an axis.

Rplot_set_axis_linear_threshold.doc: R_PLOT_SCALE_SYMLOG: the axis is linear from -threshold to threshold (default 1).

Rplot_set_axis_range.doc: Shows this range of an axis; the axis then stops following the data.

Rplot_get_axis_range.doc: The range an axis shows now (after the user moved or zoomed it).

Rplot_set_axis_auto_fit.doc: The axis is fitted to the data whenever it changes (the default, until the view is moved; a double click turns it on again).

Rplot_set_axis_format.doc: How the labels of an axis are written: a printf format for one double ("%.1f s", "%g"), NULL: chosen from the ticks.

Rplot_set_axis_visible.doc: 1: shown, 0: hidden, -1: R_PLOT_X and R_PLOT_Y always, the second axes when something uses them (the default).

Rplot_set_axis_grid.doc: Lines across the data at the ticks of an axis (on for R_PLOT_X and R_PLOT_Y).

Rplot_set_axis_inverted.doc: The values grow the other way (to the left, or down).

Rplot_set_axis_locked.doc: The user cannot move or zoom this axis (the application still can).

Rplot_fit.doc: Fits every axis that is not locked to the data, and has them follow it again (what a double click does).

Rplot_set_crosshair.doc: Lines across the data through the pointer.

Rplot_set_mouse_text.doc: The coordinates of the pointer in a corner of the data (on by default).

Rplot_set_tooltips.doc: The values of the point under the pointer, written next to it (on by default).

Rplot_get_mouse_position.doc: Where the pointer is, in the units of R_PLOT_X and R_PLOT_Y. Returns R_TRUE when it is over the data.

Rplot_data_to_point.doc: Where a point of the data (R_PLOT_X, R_PLOT_Y) is in the widget, in logical units from its corner.

Rplot_point_to_data.doc: The data (R_PLOT_X, R_PLOT_Y) at a point of the widget, in logical units from its corner.

Rplot_add_drag_line.doc:
Adds a line across the data that the user drags: vertical at an X
(axis R_PLOT_X or R_PLOT_X2), horizontal at a Y (R_PLOT_Y or R_PLOT_Y2).
Its value is written on it, after `label` (may be NULL). Returns its index.

Rplot_set_drag_line_color.doc: The color of a drag line (by default the accent of the theme).

Rchart_create.doc: A chart of a kind (Rwidget_create(R_WIDGET_CHART) makes a pie).

Rchart_set_title.doc: The title over a pie, a donut or a heatmap, under the value of a gauge (a sparkline only tells it to screen readers).

Rchart_set_format.doc:
How the values are written (the gauge, the middle of a donut, what
the pointer shows): a printf format for one double with its unit, "%.0f%%",
"$%.2f". NULL: whole numbers as they are, others with up to two decimals.

Rchart_set_color.doc: The color of the arc of a gauge outside any band, and of the line of a sparkline (default: the accent).

Rchart_set_legend.doc: The legend: the slices beside a pie or a donut, the scale of colors under a heatmap (shown by default).

Rchart_clear.doc: Removes the slices, the bands, the grid and the values.

Rchart_get_hovered.doc:
What is under the pointer: a slice, a point of a sparkline, or a
cell of a heatmap as row * columns + column; -1 for nothing.

Rchart_add_slice.doc: Adds a slice (a value of 0 or more). Returns its index, -1 when the value is not valid.

Rchart_set_slice_color.doc: The color of a slice; an alpha of 0 gives it back its color of the palette.

Rchart_get_total.doc: The sum of the values of the slices.

Rchart_set_selected.doc: The slice lifted as selected, or -1 for none (the user selects one with a click).

Rchart_set_hole.doc: The hole of a donut, as a part of its radius, from 0.2 to 0.9 (default 0.62).

Rchart_set_center_text.doc:
What the middle of a donut shows when the pointer is not over a
slice: `text` in large (NULL or "": the total) over `caption` in small
(NULL or "": none).

Rchart_set_range.doc:
The range of a gauge (default 0 to 100), and a fixed range for the
colors of a heatmap and the height of a sparkline, which otherwise follow
their values. min == max goes back to these defaults.

Rchart_get_range.doc: The range in use now (a gauge's, or the one of the values of a heatmap or a sparkline).

Rchart_set_value.doc: The value of a gauge, kept within its range when drawn.

Rchart_add_band.doc:
Colors a part of the range of a gauge (an alpha of 0: the success,
warning and danger colors of the theme, one after the other). The arc
takes the color of the band its value is in. Returns the index of the band.

Rchart_set_grid.doc:
The cells of a heatmap: `rows` x `columns` values, row after row,
copied (NULL: all 0). NaN leaves a cell empty.

Rchart_set_row_labels.doc: The names of the rows, separated by '|': "Mon|Tue|Wed" (shown at their left).

Rchart_set_column_labels.doc: The names of the columns, separated by '|' (shown over them, as many as fit).

Rchart_get_row_label.doc: The name of a row or of a column, "" when it has none.

Rchart_set_color_scale.doc: The colors of the lowest and of the highest values of a heatmap (default: a tint of the accent, the accent).

Rchart_set_values.doc: The values of a sparkline, copied. NaN leaves a gap.

Rchart_push_value.doc: Adds a value after the others, for live data; only the last `max_count` are kept (0: all of them).

Rchart_set_fill.doc: Shades the area under the line of a sparkline (on by default).

Rchart_set_marker.doc: A dot on the last value of a sparkline (on by default).

Rpdf_is_available.doc: R_TRUE when PDFium can be loaded (it is, the first time this is asked).

Rpdf_view_load_file.doc:
Shows a PDF file. `password` may be NULL. Returns R_FALSE when it
cannot: Rpdf_view_get_status tells why (a password is needed, not a
PDF, no PDFium). The view then shows that instead of pages.

Rpdf_view_load_memory.doc: Same as Rpdf_view_load_file, from bytes in memory (copied).

Rpdf_view_close.doc: Closes the document: the view is empty.

Rpdf_view_get_page_size.doc: Size of a page in points (1/72 inch), as it is shown (its rotation applied).

Rpdf_view_set_page.doc: Scrolls to the top of a page; it becomes the current page.

Rpdf_view_get_page.doc: The current page: the one a third down the view.

Rpdf_view_set_zoom.doc: A zoom of its own (1: the printed size): the fit becomes R_PDF_FIT_NONE.

Rpdf_view_get_zoom.doc: The zoom the pages show at, the one a fit gives included.

Rpdf_view_get_title.doc: The title of the document (its information), "" when it has none.

Rpdf_view_get_page_text.doc:
The text of a page (UTF-8), to search it or copy it. Valid until
the next call for this view.

Rcarousel_set_page.doc:
Shows a page, gliding to it when `animated` (and the animations
are on), at once otherwise. The page changed callback is not called.

Rcarousel_get_page.doc: The page shown, -1 when the carousel has none.

Rcarousel_next.doc: Glides to the next / previous page; nothing at the last / first one unless it loops.

Rcarousel_set_loop.doc: R_TRUE: after the last page comes the first one, and before the first the last (default R_FALSE).

Rcarousel_set_autoplay.doc:
Goes to the next page by itself every `seconds` (0: never, the
default); after the last page it comes back to the first. It waits
while the pointer is on the carousel, while the pages are dragged and
while the keyboard is in it; a page chosen by the user starts the
interval again.

Rcarousel_set_indicators_visible.doc: The dots along the bottom edge (the right edge when vertical), one per page (default R_TRUE).

Rcarousel_set_arrows_visible.doc: The previous / next buttons shown while the pointer is on the carousel (default R_TRUE).

Rcarousel_set_orientation.doc: R_HORIZONTAL: the pages side by side (default); R_VERTICAL: one above the other.

Rpdf_view_print.doc: Prints the document shown (see Rpdf_print); the job is named after its title.

Rmap_view_set_center.doc: Centers the map on a place. The latitude is held within +/-85.0511; the longitude wraps.

Rmap_view_get_center.doc: The place at the middle of the map (longitude from -180 to 180).

Rmap_view_set_zoom.doc: The zoom: 0 shows the whole world in one tile, each step doubles the scale. Fractions are allowed.

Rmap_view_set_zoom_range.doc: The zooms the user can reach (default 0 to 19, at most 0 to 24). Tiles are asked for at whole zooms of this range.

Rmap_view_animate_to.doc: Glides to a place and a zoom (at once when animations are off).

Rmap_view_screen_to_latlon.doc: The place at a point of the widget.

Rmap_view_latlon_to_screen.doc: Where a place is in the widget (of the copies of the world side by side, the one nearest the middle).

Rmap_view_set_tile_callback.doc:
Called once for each tile the map needs. Answer with
Rmap_view_set_tile, Rmap_view_set_tile_data or Rmap_view_set_tile_failed,
at once or later. Setting it forgets the tiles of the previous source.

Rmap_view_set_tile_cancel_callback.doc: Called when a tile asked for and not answered yet is no longer wanted (the user went elsewhere). Optional.

Rmap_view_set_tile.doc:
The pixels of a tile: `width` x `height` RGBA8, tightly packed
(they are copied; any size, shown at the tile size). Thread-safe: from
another thread it is applied on the UI thread during the next frame.

Rmap_view_set_tile_data.doc: A tile as the bytes of an image file (PNG, JPEG...), decoded on the calling thread. Thread-safe.

Rmap_view_set_tile_failed.doc: There is no such tile: the coarser one stays shown in its place. Thread-safe.

Rmap_view_set_tile_path.doc:
Reads the tiles from files instead of asking for them: a path
where {z}, {x} and {y} are replaced ({-y}: the row counted from the
south, as in TMS and MBTiles). The files are read and decoded on a
worker thread; a missing file is a tile that failed. NULL or "": the
tile callback again. Local files only.

Rmap_view_set_tile_size.doc: Logical size of a tile at a whole zoom (default 256, from 16 to 1024): larger tiles show the map larger.

Rmap_view_set_cache_size.doc: Memory the decoded tiles may take, in bytes (default 64 MiB). The tiles on screen are always kept.

Rmap_view_get_cache_usage.doc: Memory the decoded tiles take now, in bytes.

Rmap_view_clear_tiles.doc: Forgets every tile (they are asked for again): the tiles of the source changed.

Rmap_view_add_marker.doc: Adds a pin at a place, with a label written next to it (may be NULL). Returns its id (from 1), or -1.

Rmap_view_set_marker_color.doc: The color of a pin (by default the accent of the theme).

Rmap_view_set_attribution.doc:
A line written in the bottom right corner: the credit most tile
licences ask for, such as "(c) OpenStreetMap contributors". NULL or "": none.

Rpdf_document_set_title.doc: The information of the document, shown by readers (the title in their window).

Rpdf_document_add_page.doc: Adds a page of a size in points; drawing goes to it. Returns its index, -1 for an invalid size.

Rpdf_document_set_line_width.doc: Width of the lines and outlines, in points (default 1).

Rpdf_document_draw_rect.doc: A rectangle, its corners rounded by `radius`; `paint` is a bitmask of RPdfPaint.

Rpdf_document_draw_line.doc: A line in the stroke color.

Rpdf_document_add_font.doc:
Adds a TrueType font (.ttf) to the document (the data is
copied, and embedded in the file). Returns its number for
Rpdf_document_set_font, -1 when it is not a TrueType font.

Rpdf_document_set_font.doc: The font of the text drawn next: an RPdfFont or a number of Rpdf_document_add_font, a size in points, a bitmask of RPdfTextStyle.

Rpdf_document_get_line_height.doc: Distance between two lines of text in the current font.

Rpdf_document_measure_text.doc: Width of a text in the current font, in points (of its widest line).

Rpdf_document_draw_text.doc:
Text in the fill color, the top of its first line at y ('\n'
starts a line below). Returns its width.

Rpdf_document_draw_paragraph.doc:
Text wrapped at the spaces to fit `width`, each line placed by
`align` (R_HALIGN_LEFT, R_HALIGN_CENTER or R_HALIGN_RIGHT). Returns the
height it took.

Rpdf_document_draw_image.doc:
A picture of RGBA8 pixels stretched over a rectangle. A width or
height of 0 keeps the proportions of the picture; both 0: 96 pixels per inch.

Rpdf_document_draw_window.doc:
What a window shows (Rwindow_capture), as a picture: a report of
the screen, a chart. A width and height of 0: the size it has on the
screen. Returns R_FALSE when the window cannot be captured.

Rpdf_document_save.doc: Writes the file. Returns R_FALSE when it cannot be written.

Rpdf_document_save_memory.doc: The file in memory (followed by a '\0' not counted), to release with Rmemory_free; `size` receives its length.

Rpdf_print.doc:
Prints a PDF document with the print system: on macOS the print
panel, on Windows the print dialog (the pages are drawn by PDFium, see
PDF VIEW), on Linux and the other systems CUPS (lp or lpr) after a
dialog of Raven that chooses the printer. It waits until the job is
sent. `desc` may be NULL. Returns R_FALSE when cancelled or when it
cannot print. Not in the browser.

Rpdf_document_print.doc: Prints a document written by the application.

Rtext_editor_set_text.doc: Replaces the whole text. The history of undo is cleared; the changed callback is not called.

Rtext_editor_get_text.doc: Returns The whole text, lines separated by '\n'. Valid until the next call or the next edit.

Rtext_editor_get_length.doc: Returns The number of bytes of Rtext_editor_get_text.

Rtext_editor_get_line.doc: Returns One line, without its line break. Valid until the next edit. NULL when `line` is out of range.

Rtext_editor_insert_text.doc:
Types a text at the cursor, replacing the selection, as the user
would: it can be undone and the changed callback is called.

Rtext_editor_select.doc: Selects from one position to another; the cursor is on the second.

Rtext_editor_get_selection.doc: Start and end of the selection, in the order of the text. Returns R_FALSE when nothing is selected.

Rtext_editor_get_selected_text.doc: Returns The selected text, "" when there is none. Valid until the next call or the next edit.

Rtext_editor_scroll_to_line.doc: Scrolls so that a line is visible.

Rtext_editor_set_read_only.doc: A read-only editor can still be scrolled, selected and copied.

Rtext_editor_set_word_wrap.doc: Long lines continue on the next row instead of scrolling sideways. Off by default.

Rtext_editor_set_line_numbers.doc: Shows the line numbers in a margin. Off by default.

Rtext_editor_set_tab_size.doc: Width of a tab, in spaces (4 by default).

Rtext_editor_set_tab_inserts_spaces.doc: R_TRUE makes the Tab key insert spaces instead of a tab character. Off by default.

Rtext_editor_set_syntax.doc: The same as Rtext_editor_set_language with "XML", "C" or NULL.

Rtext_editor_set_font.doc:
R_INVALID_ID uses the font of the theme (or the fixed-width
font, with a language).
0 uses the font size of the theme.

Rtext_editor_set_placeholder.doc: Text shown, dimmed, while the editor is empty.

Rtext_editor_set_zoom.doc:
Zoom of the text: a factor of its font size, 1 = 100 % (0.5 .. 4).
The user zooms with Ctrl + wheel (around the pointer), Ctrl + '+',
Ctrl + '-' and Ctrl + 0 (back to 100 %), keypad included. Set by the
program, the top of the view stays and the zoom callback is not called.
XML: Zoom="1.25".

Rtext_editor_set_zoomable.doc: R_FALSE: Ctrl + wheel and the keys do not zoom (the wheel scrolls). On by default. XML: Zoomable="false".

Rlanguage_register.doc:
Declares a language, or replaces the one that has this name: to
add words to a built-in language, read it with Rlanguage_get, change
what you want and register it again. The strings are copied.

Rlanguage_get.doc: Reads the description of a language. The strings belong to the library. Returns R_FALSE when it is unknown.

Rlanguage_for_file.doc: Returns The name of the language of a file, from its extension, or NULL.

Rtext_editor_set_language.doc:
Gives the editor a language, by name ("C++", "Python"...), by
another usual name ("cpp", "js") or by the extension of its files
("rs"). NULL or "" removes it. An editor with a language uses the
fixed-width font unless it was given a font.

Rtext_editor_get_language.doc: Returns The name of the language of the editor, or "".

Rtext_editor_set_markdown.doc:
R_TRUE makes the editor an editor of Markdown (the "Markdown"
language; Markdown="true" in XML): the text stays as it is written,
and what it formats shows while typing, strong text in bold,
emphasized text in italic, titles in bold, code, links and marks in
their colors. A label with Rlabel_set_markdown shows the same text
formatted. R_FALSE removes the language.

Rtext_editor_get_token.doc:
What the language of the editor makes of the character at a
position: the colors come from it. R_TOKEN_TEXT without a language.

Rtext_editor_set_completion.doc: R_FALSE stops the editor from proposing words by itself; Ctrl+Space still does. On by default.

Rtext_editor_show_completions.doc: Proposes words for what is before the cursor, as Ctrl+Space does.

Rtext_editor_add_completion.doc:
Adds a proposal. Only from a completion callback. Proposals that
do not start with the prefix are left out; the others keep the order
they were added in.
A few words shown beside it ("function", "int"), or NULL.

Rtext_editor_add_completion_insert.doc:
Adds a proposal that writes another text than the one it shows
and is matched on: "Threshold", listed and filtered as such, that
writes "Threshold(" when chosen. Only from a completion callback.
What replaces the word being typed; NULL or "" is `text`.

Rtext_editor_set_completion_words.doc:
R_FALSE leaves the words of the language and the names of the
text out of the proposals: only the completion callback's are listed
(a language server that knows better). On by default.

Rtext_editor_set_auto_pairs.doc:
R_FALSE stops the editor from closing brackets and quotes and
from indenting after them. On by default; it only acts with a language.

Rtext_editor_add_marker.doc:
Underlines a part of a line and attaches a message to it, shown
when the pointer rests there: an error of a compiler, a warning.
Markers follow their line when text is added or removed above it, and
go away when their own line is edited.
-1 for the end of the line.

Rtheme_set_token_color.doc:
Color of a kind of token in the theme in use, instead of the
one Raven picks for dark and for light themes. Theme files set them
with <Syntax Keyword="#FF7AB2" String="..."/>.

Rtheme_clear_token_colors.doc: Back to the colors Raven picks.

Rheader_bar_create.doc: Text shown in the bar; NULL shows the title of the window.

Rheader_bar_set_title.doc: NULL shows the title of the window.

Rheader_bar_set_buttons.doc: Bitmask of RHeaderButtons. All by default; the maximize button only shows on a resizable window.

Rheader_bar_set_button_side.doc:
R_HALIGN_RIGHT: minimize, maximize, close, as on Windows.
R_HALIGN_LEFT: three round colored buttons, as on macOS. Until it is
set, the side is the one of the system the program runs on (left on
macOS, right elsewhere), whatever the look.

Rheader_bar_set_title_notch.doc:
R_TRUE: the title sits in a dark tab hanging from the top edge of
the bar (slanted sides, round bottom corners). XML: TitleStyle="Notch".

Rheader_bar_set_background.doc:
R_FALSE removes the background of the bar: for a header that
floats above the content (in an Overlay) or sits inside a glass panel.

Rdock_area_add_panel.doc:
Adds a panel. The dock area takes ownership of the widget.
Text of its tab.
Where it goes.
A panel of the area to split or to share tabs with, or
R_INVALID_ID for the whole area (with R_DOCK_TAB: the
first group of tabs).
Part of the split space given to the new panel, 0..1
(0 = a half, or a quarter along the whole area).

Rdock_area_move_panel.doc: Moves a panel of the area somewhere else in it.

Rdock_area_close_panel.doc: Removes a panel and deletes it.

Rdock_area_set_panel_icon.doc:
Icon drawn before the title of the tab of a panel (and on the chip while it is dragged).
Texture of the icon, R_INVALID_ID removes it.
Region of the texture (0, 0, 1, 1 : all of it).
R_TRUE: the texture is a mask drawn in the text color of the tab (monochrome icons).

Rdock_area_set_panel_closable.doc: R_FALSE removes the close button of the tab of a panel. Panels can be closed by default.

Rdock_area_hide_panel.doc:
Takes a panel out of the arrangement without deleting it (a
window of an application closed from its menu). Its tab disappears
and its neighbours take its place; the area remembers where it was.

Rdock_area_open_panel.doc: Puts a hidden panel back where it was, and brings its tab to the front (also for a panel that is not hidden).

Rdock_area_is_panel_open.doc: Returns R_TRUE when the panel is in the arrangement (not hidden), shown or behind another tab.

Rdock_area_set_close_hides.doc:
R_TRUE: the close button of a tab hides its panel
(Rdock_area_hide_panel) instead of deleting it. XML: CloseHides="true".
The close callback is asked first either way.

Rdock_area_show_panel.doc: Brings the tab of a panel to the front.

Rdock_area_is_panel_shown.doc: Returns R_TRUE when the panel is the one shown in its group of tabs.

Rdock_area_set_movable.doc: R_FALSE stops the user from moving the panels (the borders can still be dragged).

Rdock_area_save_layout.doc:
Describes how the panels are arranged, as a short text to keep
in a settings file. Panels are named by their widget name
(Rwidget_set_name): unnamed panels are not part of the description.
Returns A string valid until the next call.

Rdock_area_load_layout.doc:
Arranges the panels as a saved description says. Panels of the
area that the description does not name keep a place; names it has
that match no panel are ignored in legacy descriptions. Versioned
descriptions with floating cards reject unknown or duplicate names.
