Returns R_FALSE when the text is not a layout (nothing is changed).

Rdock_area_set_tearable.doc:
Tearing: a tab dragged out of the area takes its panel to a
window of its own (a floating area of the same family), and a tab
dragged from such a window over the area docks it back where it is
dropped. A double click on the tab of a floating window, or closing
that window, puts its panels back where they were. Dragging the only
tab of a floating window moves the window. R_TRUE by default; XML:
Tearable="false". The functions of this area that take a panel also
work on its panels that are in floating windows.

Rdock_area_set_float_mode.doc: Default for future floats/tears; existing floating panels keep their mode.

Rdock_area_set_float_window.doc:
How the windows of torn-off panels are made (native windows,
R_DOCK_FLOAT_WINDOW; in-window cards are not windows).
RWindowFlags they are created with: R_WINDOW_NO_RESIZE,
R_WINDOW_BORDERLESS, R_WINDOW_CUSTOM_HEADER and
R_WINDOW_TRANSPARENT (the others are ignored).
R_WINDOW_DEFAULT by default.
May be NULL: the floating area is the whole window.
Dragging the only tab of such a window still moves it, and closing
it (its header bar's close button too) docks its panels back.

Rdock_area_float_panel.doc: Floats a panel. Native mode: screen x/y; in-window mode: window-local logical x/y. Returns its containing window.

Rdock_area_dock_panel.doc: A floating panel goes back where it was in the area.

Rdock_area_get_panel_window.doc: The window a floating panel is in, R_INVALID_ID when it is docked in the area.

Risland_set_expanded.doc: Unfolds or folds the island. The changed callback is not called.

Risland_expand_for.doc:
Unfolds the island, and folds it back by itself after a while:
to tell something to the user. It stays open while the pointer is on it.

Risland_set_expand_on_hover.doc: R_TRUE (default): the island unfolds under the pointer and folds back when it leaves.

Risland_set_expand_on_click.doc: R_TRUE (default): a click on the island unfolds or folds it.

Risland_set_attached.doc:
R_TRUE gives the island square upper corners: a notch that hangs
from the edge it touches, instead of a capsule that floats under it.

Risland_set_notch.doc:
R_TRUE: on a screen with a camera housing at its top (the notch
of a MacBook), the island of a window (Rwindow_set_island) lives in the
housing itself, in a window of its own anchored to the screen: it stays
there when the window is moved, and takes the mouse and the keyboard as
usual. Folded, it is the housing grown into two ears: the first Spacer
of its folded content becomes the room of the camera (what is before
it shows on the left, what is after on the right). Unfolded, its
content starts under the camera.

It is in the housing while its window is the last one of the
application the user worked in, is shown, and is on that screen; it
goes back into its window otherwise, and on the window systems and
screens without a housing (where nothing changes). XML: Notch="true".

Risland_is_in_notch.doc: R_TRUE while the island is in the camera housing of the screen.

Rwindow_set_island.doc:
Shows a widget (usually an island) floating at the top of a
window, in the middle, above its content. The window takes ownership;
the previous one is deleted. R_INVALID_ID removes it. The padding of
its slot (Rslot_set_padding) is its distance from the top edge.

Rwindow_set_taskbar_progress.doc:
A progress bar on the icon of the application: on the button of
the window in the taskbar (Windows), on the icon in the Dock (macOS),
on the launcher (Linux). There is one icon for the whole application in
the Dock and the launchers: the last window that set it is shown.
From 0 to 1 (not used by NONE and INDETERMINATE).
Returns R_FALSE where the system shows no progress.

Rwindow_request_attention.doc:
Asks the user to look at the window when it is not the active
one: its taskbar button flashes (Windows), the icon bounces in the
Dock (macOS), the window is marked urgent (X11, the launchers of
Linux). `critical`: until the user comes to the window; otherwise a few
times. Nothing happens when the window is already the active one.

Rtaskbar_set_badge.doc:
A short text on the icon of the application: a number of unread
messages, "!". macOS: the badge of the Dock. Windows: a small round
icon on the taskbar buttons of the windows, drawn from the text (one
to three characters fit). Linux: a number only (the text is read as
one; anything else shows nothing). NULL or "": no badge.

Rtaskbar_set_menu.doc:
The menu of the icon of the application in the Dock (macOS),
above the entries of the system. A MENU without a parent: its
MenuItems fire as when chosen in a window (clicked callback, action),
and what changes in it shows the next time the menu opens.
R_INVALID_ID: none. R_FALSE where the system has no such menu.

Rtaskbar_set_jump_list.doc:
The tasks of the jump list of Windows (right click on the button
of the application in the taskbar, or on its tile in the Start menu).
Choosing one starts the application again with its arguments: the
application reads them as any other command line. count 0: none.
R_FALSE where there is no jump list.

Rtray_is_supported.doc:
Returns R_TRUE when the system shows tray icons: always on Windows and
macOS; on Linux, when a host of StatusNotifierItem runs (the panel of
the desktop). An icon made where none runs yet appears when one starts.

Rtray_create.doc:
Puts an icon of the application beside the clock. While one
exists, the application goes on running when its last window closes
(Ris_running): Rquit (or the action app.quit) ends it.
Returns R_INVALID_ID where the system has none.

Rtray_set_icon.doc:
The picture, from tightly packed RGBA8 pixels (straight alpha);
the system scales it (16 to 32 pixels square fit everywhere). Copied.

Rtray_set_tooltip.doc: The text shown when the pointer rests on the icon (and its title for the Linux panels).

Rtray_set_menu.doc:
The menu the system shows for the icon: on a right click
(Windows, Linux), on a click (macOS). A MENU without a parent, whose
MenuItems fire as when chosen in a window; what changes in it shows
the next time it opens. R_INVALID_ID: none.

Rtray_set_clicked_callback.doc:
Called on a click: the left button (activate), the right one
when there is no menu, the middle one. On macOS an icon with a menu
opens it instead.

Rtray_set_title.doc:
A short text shown beside the icon (macOS menu bar), drawn by the
system in its own font and colors; the item widens to fit it. NULL or
"": the icon alone. Systems that show no text there ignore it (the
tooltip is the place for it).

Rtray_get_rect.doc:
Where the icon is on the screen, in the units and coordinates of
Rwindow_set_position (a window can then open just under it).
Returns R_FALSE when the system does not tell (the outputs are then 0).

Rcolor_picker_set_color.doc: Sets the color (0..1 each). The callback is not called.

Rcolor_picker_set_hsv.doc:
The same color as hue (0..360), saturation and value (0..1).
The picker remembers the hue of a gray and the saturation of black,
which red, green and blue cannot tell.

Rcolor_picker_set_hex.doc:
Sets the color from text: "#RGB", "#RRGGBB", "#RRGGBBAA" (the
'#' may be left out) or one of the color names of the XML attributes.
A code without opacity leaves the opacity as it is.
Returns R_FALSE when the text is not a color (the color is unchanged).

Rcolor_picker_get_hex.doc: Returns "#RRGGBB", or "#RRGGBBAA" when the opacity is shown and not full. Valid until the color changes.

Rcolor_picker_set_alpha_enabled.doc: R_TRUE (default) shows the opacity strip and the fourth number. R_FALSE: colors are opaque.

Rcolor_picker_set_previous_color.doc:
The color shown next to the current one, to compare with what
was there before: clicking it comes back to it. Rcolor_picker_set_color
does not change it; a popup picker takes it when it opens.

Rcolor_picker_add_swatch.doc: Adds a color to the row of swatches: one click takes it.

Rcolor_picker_set_popup.doc: R_TRUE turns the widget into a swatch that opens the picker in a popup.

Rcolor_picker_set_compact.doc: R_TRUE hides the code and the numbers: only the square, the strips and the swatches.

Rcolor_rgb_to_hsv.doc: Red, green, blue (0..1) to hue (0..360), saturation, value (0..1).

Rtimeline_set_duration.doc: Length of the sequence. The view and the playhead stay within 0 .. duration.

Rtimeline_set_time.doc: Moves the playhead. The time callback is not called.

Rtimeline_set_snapping.doc: R_FALSE lets items be placed anywhere (holding Alt while dragging does it for one move).

Rtimeline_set_view.doc: The part of the sequence that is shown. Zooming is showing less.

Rtimeline_set_playing.doc:
Makes the playhead run by itself, at the speed of the clock,
calling the time callback at each frame; at the end it stops, or
starts again with Rtimeline_set_loop.

Rtimeline_set_header_width.doc: Width of the column of the names of the tracks. 0 (default): fits the longest name.

Rtimeline_get_header_width.doc: Returns The width of the column of the names, as laid out now.

Rtimeline_set_ruler_height.doc: Height of the ruler of time (and of the markers' flags band). 0 (default): automatic.

Rtimeline_set_default_track_height.doc: Height of the tracks that have none of their own (Rtimeline_set_track_height). 0 (default): automatic.

Rtimeline_add_track.doc: Returns The track, or 0. Tracks are shown in the order they were added.

Rtimeline_remove_track.doc: Removes a track and everything on it.

Rtimeline_get_track.doc: Returns The index-th track from the top, or 0.

Rtimeline_set_track_color.doc: Color of the clips and keys of the track that have none of their own.

Rtimeline_set_track_height.doc: Height of the track in logical units; 0 = the default.

Rtimeline_set_track_locked.doc: A locked track shows its items but does not let the user change them.

Rtimeline_set_track_muted.doc: A muted track is drawn dimmed; what muting means is up to the application.

Rtimeline_set_track_style.doc:
A property of the look of a track: "ClipStyle" (Solid,
Gradient, Tint, Outline), "KeyShape" (Diamond, Circle, Square...),
"KeySize", "ClipRadius", "Background" (its lane), or a part and a
property ("Clip.Glow", "Key.BorderColor"). "" or "Default" gives back
the one of the timeline.
Returns R_FALSE when the name or the value is not one.

Rtimeline_add_clip.doc: Returns The clip, or 0 when the track does not exist.

Rtimeline_add_marker.doc: A named moment of the whole sequence, shown on the ruler and across the tracks.

Rtimeline_clear.doc: Removes every track, clip, key and marker.

Rtimeline_get_item_track.doc: Returns The track of a clip or of a key; 0 for a marker.

Rtimeline_get_item_length.doc: Returns The length of a clip; 0 for a key or a marker.

Rtimeline_set_item.doc: Moves an item: to another track (0 = keep), another start, another length (clips; negative = keep).

Rtimeline_set_item_style.doc:
A property of the look of one clip, key or marker: "Style"
(Solid, Gradient, Tint, Outline: clips), "Shape" (keys), or any
property of its part ("Background", "BorderColor", "Glow",
"CornerRadius", "Foreground" for its label...).

Rtimeline_set_preset.doc: The look the timeline starts from (R_PRESET_AUTO by default; Preset="..." in XML).

Rtimeline_get_item.doc: Returns The index-th item, in the order they were added, or 0.

Rtimeline_select.doc: Selects an item, alone or (add) with the ones already selected.

Rtimeline_set_changed_callback.doc:
Called for each item the user moved, stretched or retimed, as
it happens. The action of the widget (OnChanged in XML) fires once
per gesture, when the button is released.

Rtimeline_set_selection_callback.doc: Called when the selection changed; `item` is the item just clicked, or 0.

Rtimeline_set_activated_callback.doc: Called when an item is double-clicked.

Rtimeline_set_removed_callback.doc:
Called when the user deletes an item (the Delete key), before
it is removed: its values can still be read. Without this callback the
Delete key does nothing: the application decides what can be deleted.

Rnode_graph_add_node.doc: Top-left corner of the node, in the units of the canvas.

Rnode_graph_remove_node.doc: Removes a node, its pins, their links, and the widget it holds.

Rnode_graph_get_node_size.doc: Size of a node on the canvas: Raven works it out from its title, its pins and its content.

Rnode_graph_set_node_color.doc: Color of the header of the node; without one it takes the accent color of the theme.

Rnode_graph_set_node_style.doc:
A property of the look of one node: "HeaderStyle" (Solid,
Gradient, Stripe, Tint, None), "HeaderColor", "TitleColor",
"Background", "BorderColor", "BorderWidth", "CornerRadius", "Glow",
"Icon" (an image file shown before its title), or a part and a property
("Header.Gradient", "Node.ShadowSize"). "" or "Default" gives back the
one of the graph.
Returns R_FALSE when the name or the value is not one.

Rnode_graph_set_node_content.doc:
Puts a widget inside the node, under its pins: the graph owns
it from now on. R_INVALID_ID removes (and deletes) the one it had.

Rnode_graph_set_node_name.doc:
Name of the node, the `Name` of its XML element: what
<Link From="name.pin"> and Rnode_graph_find_node look for. Not shown.

Rnode_graph_find_node.doc: Returns The node of that name, or 0.

Rnode_graph_set_node_user_data.doc: Value the application attaches to a node.

Rnode_graph_add_input.doc: Free text, or NULL for a pin that links to any type. return The pin, or 0.

Rnode_graph_set_pin_name.doc: Name of the pin for Rnode_graph_find_pin and for the links of XML; a pin without one answers to its label.

Rnode_graph_find_pin.doc: Returns The pin of a node with that name (or label), or 0.

Rnode_graph_get_pin_position.doc: Where a pin is on the canvas (the middle of its dot).

Rnode_graph_get_input.doc: Returns The index-th input (or output) of a node, or 0.

Rnode_graph_set_type_color.doc: Color of the pins of a type and of the links between them.

Rnode_graph_set_type_style.doc:
A property of the pins of a type and of their links: "Shape"
(Circle, Ring, Square, Diamond, Triangle, Arrow), "Size", "Glow",
"LinkShape" (Bezier, Straight, Step, Angled), "LinkWidth", "LinkGlow".

Rnode_graph_connect.doc:
Links an output to an input, as the user does by dragging.
The connect callback is not asked.
Returns The link; 0 when the pins cannot be linked (two inputs, the
same node, different types).

Rnode_graph_get_input_link.doc: Returns The link that arrives at an input pin, or 0.

Rnode_graph_set_view.doc: What the middle of the widget shows: a point of the canvas, and how large (1 = one unit per logical unit).

Rnode_graph_to_canvas.doc: Converts a point of the widget (from its corner, as in the events) to the canvas, and back, with the view as it is shown now.

Rnode_graph_frame_all.doc: Moves and zooms so that every node shows.

Rnode_graph_set_grid_visible.doc: R_FALSE hides the grid of dots (shown by default).

Rnode_graph_set_flow_visible.doc:
The pulses of light that run along the links, from output to
input. By default they run while the pointer is over the graph, and
the window rests the rest of the time. R_TRUE makes them run all the
time (the window then draws without pause); R_FALSE stops them.

Rnode_graph_set_read_only.doc: R_TRUE: the user can look but not move, link or delete.

Rnode_graph_set_preset.doc: The look the graph starts from (R_PRESET_AUTO by default; Preset="..." in XML).

Rnode_graph_set_linked_callback.doc: Called after the user made a link, and before a link the user removed goes (its pins can still be read).

Rnode_graph_set_moved_callback.doc: Called for each node the user moved, when the button is released.

Rnode_graph_set_selection_callback.doc: Called when the selection changed; `item` is the node just clicked, or 0.

Rnode_graph_set_removed_callback.doc:
Called when the user deletes a node (the Delete key), before
it is removed. Without this callback the Delete key only removes
links: the application decides whether nodes can be deleted.

Rnode_graph_set_activated_callback.doc: Called when the user double-clicks a node (to open what it stands for).

Rnode_graph_set_canvas_activated_callbac.doc:
Double click on the empty canvas (`item` 0): the application acts
there (a search to add a node...). Without this callback it frames all nodes.

Rnode_graph_set_wire_dropped_callback.doc:
A wire the user pulled from a pin was released on nothing: `item` is
that pin, x, y where it was dropped (to offer a node to connect it to). The
wire draws back as usual.

Rnode_graph_set_pin_clicked_callback.doc:
A pin was clicked, not dragged (`item` is the pin, x, y on the canvas):
the application may link in two clicks (Rnode_graph_set_pin_emphasis shows where
the second may go). With this callback such a click neither detaches the wire
of an input nor counts as a wire dropped on nothing.

Rnode_graph_get_node_at.doc: The node under a point of the widget (x, y as in the events: Rnode_graph_to_canvas), or 0.

Rnode_graph_get_pin_at.doc: The pin near a point of the widget (or whose tag is under it: Rnode_graph_set_pin_tag), or 0 (a menu for a pin).

Rnode_graph_get_link_at.doc: The link under a point of the widget, or 0 (hidden links are never under it).

Rnode_graph_set_pin_multiple.doc:
R_TRUE: this input keeps every link made to it (a state that several
transitions enter) instead of one. Pulling a wire from it starts a new one.

Rnode_graph_set_node_active.doc: R_TRUE: the node is running (live debug) : a soft ring breathes around it.

Rnode_graph_set_node_active_color.doc: Color of that ring (the success color of the theme by default).

Rnode_graph_set_node_deletable.doc: R_FALSE: the Delete key does not remove this node (the root of a tree, the output of a graph).

Rnode_graph_set_node_shown.doc: Shows a node at once, without the animation a node added to a shown graph pops in with (an application that rebuilds its graph).

Rnode_graph_set_link_shown.doc: The same for a link made with Rnode_graph_connect: drawn whole at once instead of growing from its output.

Rnode_graph_set_node_icon.doc: An icon before the title: a texture of the application, shared by many nodes and not deleted with them (the "Icon" style loads one per node from a file). R_INVALID_ID removes it.

Rnode_graph_set_node_badge.doc: A short text in a pill on the top right corner of the node ("1", "!"...); NULL or "" removes it.

Rnode_graph_set_pin_tag.doc:
A short text in a chip of the pin's color outside the node, beside the pin
(left of an input, right of an output): the name of what goes out or comes in
there, as a net label of a schematic. NULL or "" removes it.

Rnode_graph_set_link_hidden.doc:
R_TRUE: the link stays (its pins are linked, the application keeps
it) but is not drawn and not picked: its two ends are shown otherwise (pin
tags naming it, as the labels of a schematic stand for a wire).

Rnode_graph_set_pin_emphasis.doc:
How much a pin stands out, as while a wire is pulled: 1 shows it as a pin
to go to, -1 steps it back, 0 as usual (an application that links in two clicks).

Rnode_graph_get_tag_at.doc: The pin whose tag (Rnode_graph_set_pin_tag) is under a point of the widget, or 0: the chip only, not the pin.

Rnode_graph_set_pin_tag_lit.doc:
R_TRUE: the pin's tag is drawn as under the pointer (a stronger fill, a
thicker edge) — every tag of one net lit while the pointer is on one of them.

Rnode_graph_set_pin_label_width.doc:
Pin labels wider than `width` (logical units) are cut short with an
ellipsis and the nodes are laid out with them so (compact ports); 0, the
default, shows every label whole.

Rnode_graph_set_node_badge_color.doc: Color of the badge pill of one node (Rnode_graph_set_node_badge); its text turns dark or light to suit it. A negative component restores the look's color.

Rblock_editor_add_kind.doc: A kind of block, and its block in the palette. Returns its index, -1 on an error.

Rblock_editor_set_category_color.doc: Color of the blocks of a category (Raven picks one from its name otherwise).

Rblock_editor_add_block.doc: A new block, the top of a script of its own at x, y (canvas units). Returns it, 0 on an error.

Rblock_editor_remove_block.doc: Removes a block and everything that hangs under it.

Rblock_editor_attach.doc: Puts a block (with what is under it) at a place of another one. R_FALSE when it does not fit there.

Rblock_editor_detach.doc: Takes a block (with what is under it) out: a script of its own at x, y.

Rblock_editor_get_script.doc: The top block of a script.

Rblock_editor_get_next.doc: The block under it, 0 if none.

Rblock_editor_get_body.doc: The first block in a mouth of a C block, 0 if empty.

Rblock_editor_get_input.doc: The value block in a slot, 0 if the slot holds a typed value.

Rblock_editor_get_value.doc: The typed value of a slot.

Rblock_editor_get_parent.doc: Where a block hangs: the block it hangs from (0: the top of a script).

Rblock_editor_set_block_glow.doc: R_TRUE: the block is running: a halo breathes around it.

Rblock_editor_save.doc: Every script as text (valid until the next call).

Rblock_editor_load.doc: Replaces the scripts with those of a text from Rblock_editor_save.

Rblock_editor_set_slot_options.doc: The choices of a %m slot of a kind, separated by '\n' ("" : the slot is typed in).

Rblock_editor_set_kind_visible.doc: R_FALSE: the kind is not in the palette (its blocks stay where they are).

Rblock_editor_set_kind_label.doc:
A new label for a kind (a function that takes one more input...).
The blocks of that kind keep the values of the slots that are still there.

Rblock_editor_set_block_deletable.doc: R_FALSE: the user cannot delete the block (the entry of a function). Not saved.

Rblock_editor_select.doc: Selects a block (add: R_FALSE clears the selection first ; block 0 : only clears).

Rblock_editor_get_view.doc: Pan (canvas units at the top left) and zoom.

Rdialog_open.doc:
Shows a widget as a dialog of a window. The window takes
ownership of `content`: it is deleted when the dialog closes, so read
what you need from it before, or in `closed`.
The Escape key dismisses the dialog (result 0).

Rdialog_close.doc:
Closes the dialog that contains a widget (the content itself or
anything inside it: the button that was clicked).
Passed to the closed callback and returned by Rdialog_run.

Rdialog_run.doc: Shows a dialog and waits until it closes. Returns its result.

Rpopup_open.doc:
Shows a widget as a popup over the window, its top-left corner at
x, y (window coordinates; moved to stay inside the window): a search box,
a palette, a picker. Unlike a dialog it does not block the window: a click
outside it, or Escape, closes it. The application keeps the content (it is
not deleted on close) and can open it again. `closed` (may be NULL) is
called when it closes, with the result given to Rpopup_close (0 when dismissed).
The content draws its own background (a Border with a Background...).

Rpopup_close.doc: Closes the popup that contains a widget (the content or anything inside it).

Rpopup_is_open.doc: Returns R_TRUE while the widget is shown as a popup.

Rwindow_has_dialog.doc: Returns R_TRUE while a dialog is shown in the window.

Rmessage_box.doc:
Shows a message with buttons and waits for the answer.
R_INVALID_ID: the first window of the application.
May be NULL.

Rfile_dialog_open.doc:
Asks for a file to open.
May be NULL.
Returns The path (UTF-8), valid until the next file dialog, or NULL when the user cancelled.

Rfile_dialog_save.doc: Asks where to save a file. An existing file was confirmed by the user.

Rfile_dialog_get_result_count.doc: What the last file dialog returned: several paths with R_FILE_DIALOG_MULTIPLE.

Rfile_register_memory.doc:
Registers a file held in memory under a path: every file Raven
reads (XML documents and their Include, Source and Font attributes,
themes, textures, fonts, Rfile_read) is looked up here first, so that
resources embedded in the executable need no file beside it. A relative
path names the file as it is written in the XML once joined to the
folder of the document that names it (Rxml_set_base_path for a
document given as text), e.g. "ui/editor.xml". Paths compare with '/'
and '\\' alike. Memory files are not watched for live reload. Call it
after Rinit; Rshutdown forgets every file.
R_TRUE: Raven keeps a copy; R_FALSE: `data` must outlive Raven (static data).

Rfile_is_memory.doc: R_TRUE when `path` is a file registered with Rfile_register_memory.

Rfile_read.doc:
Whole files, with UTF-8 paths on every platform.
On Android and iOS, a relative path that names no file held in memory
and no file on disk is read from the app's package (the APK's assets/,
the bundle's resources), and so is every file Raven reads by its path.
Returns Rfile_read: the content followed by a '\0', to release with
Rmemory_free; NULL when the file cannot be read. `size` may be NULL.

Rfile_browser_set_directory.doc: Shows a folder. "~" is the home of the user. Returns R_FALSE when it cannot be read.

Rfile_browser_set_filters.doc: Kinds of files the user chooses from; the first one is active. The strings are copied.

Rfile_browser_set_multiple.doc: R_TRUE lets several files be selected (Ctrl and Shift with a click).

Rfile_browser_set_controls_visible.doc:
R_FALSE hides the name field, the filter list and the buttons:
what remains is an explorer to put in a side panel. Shown by default.

Rfile_browser_set_places_visible.doc: R_FALSE hides the list of places on the left.

Rfile_browser_set_file_name.doc: Name typed in the name field (save mode).

Rfile_browser_set_default_extension.doc: Added to a name typed without extension, in save mode.

Rfile_browser_get_selection_count.doc: Paths of the selected entries. The strings are valid until the selection or the folder changes.

Rfile_browser_select.doc: Selects an entry of the folder by its name.

Rfile_browser_set_selection_changed_call.doc: Called when the selection changes; `path` is the entry under the cursor, or NULL.

Rnotification_show.doc: Returns R_TRUE when the system took the notification.

Rnotification_is_supported.doc: R_FALSE when the platform has no notifications (Rnotification_show then always uses the fallback).

Rnotification_set_fallback.doc: Called with the notifications the system could not show; NULL: none.

Rnotification_set_clicked_callback.doc:
Called when the user clicks a notification of Rnotification_show
(on the UI thread; the application may then bring its window to the
front: the system lets it). It is the last one shown that was clicked:
the application remembers what it was about. NULL: none.
Windows and macOS (elsewhere it is never called).

Rviewport_set_texture.doc: Shows a texture. R_INVALID_ID shows nothing.

Rviewport_set_stretch.doc: How the texture is fitted in the widget. Default: R_STRETCH_FILL.

Rviewport_set_flip_y.doc: R_TRUE flips the texture vertically (OpenGL framebuffers are bottom-up).

Rviewport_set_native.doc:
Creates (or destroys) the native child window of the viewport.
The viewport must already be in a window.
Returns R_TRUE on success.

Rviewport_get_native_handle.doc: Fills `native` with the handles of the child window.

Rviewport_get_pixel_size.doc: Size of the viewport in pixels after the last layout.

Rviewport_set_realtime.doc:
R_TRUE redraws the window every frame while the viewport is
visible (game view). R_FALSE redraws only on Rwidget_invalidate (default).

Rcustom_set_measure_callback.doc: Reports the desired size of the widget. Without it the widget asks for 0 x 0.

Rdraw_rect.doc: Filled rectangle with rounded corners (radius 0 = sharp).

Rdraw_shadow.doc:
Soft shadow or glow: a rounded rectangle blurred by `blur` logical units.
Offset the rectangle for a drop shadow, or draw it under a shape for a glow.
Nonpositive width, height or blur draws nothing. Uses the same primitive as Border shadows.

Rdraw_rect_outline.doc: Outline of a rounded rectangle, drawn inside its bounds.

Rdraw_curve.doc: Anti-aliased cubic Bezier curve from (x0, y0) to (x1, y1), pulled by two control points.

Rdraw_image.doc: Texture stretched to a rectangle and multiplied by a tint color.

Rdraw_text.doc:
Draws UTF-8 text; (x, y) is the top-left corner of the first line.
R_INVALID_ID uses the theme font.
0 uses R_METRIC_FONT_SIZE.

Rdraw_glass.doc:
Rounded rectangle of glass. It shows what was drawn before it,
frosted and bent along its rim, under a tint: (r, g, b) is the color of
the tint and `a` its strength (0 = clear glass, 1 = opaque color).
Works with any theme. Needs a backend that implements glass (the Vulkan
backend does).

Rdraw_spring.doc:
Animates a value from the paint callback of a custom widget.
Moves the spring toward `target` by the time elapsed since the last
frame and returns its value. While it moves, the window keeps drawing
frames by itself. The first call puts the spring on its target.

static RSpring size;                                  (zeroed)
float s = Rdraw_spring(painter, &size, hovered ? 1.0f : 0.0f, R_MOTION_BOUNCY);
Rdraw_circle(painter, cx, cy, 20.0f + 8.0f * s, ...);

Rspring_kick.doc: Pushes a spring away from its target (units per second): it bounces back.

Rspring_set.doc: Puts a spring at rest on a value, without animation.

Rdraw_push_clip_rect.doc: Restricts the following draws to a rectangle, intersected with the current one.

Rshader_create.doc:
A shader from SPIR-V code (a fragment shader written with
raven_effect.glsl, as in a .spv file): `size` bytes, copied. R_INVALID_ID
when the code is not SPIR-V; a backend that refuses it reports an error
and the effect is drawn as a rectangle.

Rshader_create_from_file.doc: The same, from a .spv file (UTF-8 path, relative to the current folder).

Reffect_get.doc: A built-in effect, created the first time it is asked for.

Reffect_find.doc: A built-in effect by its name ("aurora", "shimmer", "neon", "ripple", "plasma", "grain", "spotlight", "mesh"), or R_INVALID_ID.

Reffect_get_defaults.doc: Its colors and parameters when nothing else is given (Rshader_look_init uses them).

Rshader_look_init.doc: White to white, no parameter, no texture, square corners, animated when the shader is.

Rshader_look_defaults.doc: Fills a look with the defaults of the shader when it is a built-in effect (else Rshader_look_init).

Rdraw_shader.doc:
From a paint callback: draws the effect over a rectangle of the
widget (logical units, from its top left corner).

Rborder_set_effect.doc:
The background of a border becomes an effect (its Background,
if any, is drawn under it; its child over it). R_INVALID_ID removes it.
XML: Effect="aurora" or Effect="file.spv", EffectColor, EffectColor2,
EffectParams="a,b,c,d", EffectAnimate, EffectBackdrop (for a file).

Rwindow_create_from_xml.doc:
Creates a window from a document whose root element is <Window>.
UTF-8 text. It does not need to be null-terminated.
Size of the text in bytes.
Returns The window, or R_INVALID_ID. Parse errors are reported with
their line and column through the error callback (R_ERROR_XML).

Rwidget_create_from_xml.doc:
Creates a widget tree from a document whose root element is a
widget. The caller owns the returned widget until it is added to a parent.

Rxml_set_base_path.doc:
A folder looked into after the one of the document (see above),
and the first one for the documents given from memory. NULL or "": none.

Rxml_set_live_reload.doc:
Turns live reload on or off. It is on by default; the
environment variable RAVEN_LIVE_RELOAD=0 turns it off without
rebuilding. When off, files are never looked at again.

Rxml_check_files.doc:
Looks at the files now, without waiting for the next look
(there are five per second), even when live reload is off.
Returns The number of files found changed.

Rxml_register_widgets.doc:
Reads the <Widget Name="..."> declarations of a document (its
root, or the children of a <Widgets> root) so that the tags they
declare can be used in the documents loaded afterwards.
Returns The number of tags declared.

Rxml_get_registered_widget_count.doc: The declared tags, for tools that list them.

Rxml_register_tag.doc:
Registers a tag (or replaces what it was registered with).
Returns R_FALSE when the name is the one of a widget of Raven, or when too many tags are registered (64).

Rxml_resolve_path.doc:
The path of a file named in a document: as the attributes
Source of Raven read it, looked for where files are looked for (see
Rxml_set_base_path): the folder of the document being loaded (while it
loads) and its subfolders, the base path, the current folder, PATH.
When no place holds it, the path it would have next to the document
(else in the base path). For the attributes of the tags made by code
that name files.
Returns The path; valid until the next call.

Rwidget_set_attribute.doc:
Sets a property from text, with the names and value syntax of the
XML attributes. Handy for scripting and data-driven tools.
Returns R_TRUE when the attribute exists for this widget and the value is valid.

Rxml_document_create.doc: A new document with one element.

Rxml_document_parse.doc:
Reads a text into a document. Comments are kept.
When not NULL, a mistake in the text is described there
and nothing is reported; when NULL it goes to the error callback.
Returns The document, or R_INVALID_ID.

Rxml_document_load.doc: Reads a file. The paths written in it are relative to its folder.

Rxml_document_destroy.doc: Releases a document and its nodes. What was built from it lives on.

Rxml_document_to_string.doc:
Writes the document as text, one element per line, indented
with tabs. Rxml_node_get_line then says where each node was written.
Returns The text, valid until the next call for this document or its destruction.

Rxml_document_create_widget.doc:
Builds the widgets the document describes, as
Rwidget_create_from_xml does. When the root is a <Window>, builds what
the window would show (R_INVALID_ID when it is empty).

Rxml_document_create_window.doc: Builds the window the document describes, as Rwindow_create_from_xml does.

Rxml_node_get_tag.doc: Returns The tag of an element, "" for a comment.

Rxml_node_get_text.doc: The text inside an element (<Label>this</Label>), or the text of a comment.

Rxml_node_get_index.doc: Returns The place of a node among the children of its parent; 0 for the root.

Rxml_node_add_child.doc:
Where among the children; -1 for the end.
Returns The new node; R_INVALID_ID (R_ERROR_XML) when it would be nested
deeper than a document can be: 256 levels under the root, as
when a text is read. The same holds for the functions below.

Rxml_node_add_xml.doc:
Reads a piece of XML (one element and what it contains) and
adds it: what a palette, a paste or a template inserts.

Rxml_node_remove.doc: Removes a node and what it contains. The root stays.

Rxml_node_move.doc:
Moves a node, with what it contains, under another parent of
the same document or elsewhere under its own.
Where among the children of the new parent, counted once the node has left its place; -1 for the end.
Returns R_FALSE when it cannot be done (the root, a parent that is inside the node, or a place too deep).

Rxml_node_duplicate.doc: Copies a node and what it contains, right after it. Returns the copy.

Rxml_node_to_string.doc: The node as text. Valid until the next call for this document.

Rxml_node_get_attribute.doc: Returns The value of an attribute (names are compared without case), or NULL when the node does not have it.

Rxml_node_set_attribute.doc: Sets an attribute, added after the others when it is new. A NULL value removes it.

Rxml_node_get_line.doc:
Returns The line of the node, starting at 1, in the text the document
was read from or last written to; 0 for a node added since.

Rxml_node_get_widget.doc:
Returns The widget (the window, for a <Window>) the node became the
last time the document was built, or R_INVALID_ID: never built,
destroyed since, or not a widget (an <Item>, a comment). A tag declared
with <Widget> gives the widget it stands for.

Rwidget_get_xml_node.doc:
Returns The node a widget was built from, or R_INVALID_ID: not built
from a document, or the document is gone. The widgets inside a tag
declared with <Widget> all come from the node where the tag is used.

Rxml_get_tag_count.doc: The tags of the library, <Window> included. Those declared with <Widget> are listed by Rxml_get_registered_widget_name.

Rxml_get_tag_description.doc: Returns One line about a tag, "" when there is nothing to say.

Rxml_get_tag_children.doc: Returns 0: no child widget; 1: a single one; 2: any number. Declared and unknown tags give 2.

Rxml_get_attribute_count.doc:
The attributes of a tag: its own first, then those every widget
has, then those of its place in its parent. For a tag declared with
<Widget>, its own are its parameters.

Rscript_load.doc:
Loads a script given as text (not an XML document): its
functions become actions, its globals are initialized.
Names it in the diagnostics (a file name); may be NULL.
Returns R_FALSE when it has an error (nothing of it is installed).

Rscript_check.doc:
Checks a script, or the scripts of an XML document and the
functions its widgets name, without running anything nor building a
widget. The diagnostics are reported as usual.
A script, or an XML document (text that starts with '<').
Returns The number of errors.

Rscript_check_file.doc: Returns The number of errors in the file (a .rvs or an .xml), -1 when it cannot be read.

Rscript_format.doc:
Formats a script: one statement per line, blocks indented,
spaces around operators; comments are kept.
One level of indentation; NULL for four spaces.
Returns The text, valid until the next call; NULL when the script has a
syntax error (it is not changed).

Rscript_reset.doc: Removes every script function (their actions are unbound) and every global. Not while a script runs.

Rscript_has_function.doc: Returns R_TRUE when a script function has that name.

Rscript_set_enabled.doc:
R_FALSE: the <Script> elements of the documents are read but not
compiled nor run (a design tool that shows interfaces without running
them). On by default.

Rscript_set_limits.doc:
The limits of the scripts. 0 keeps a value.
Instructions one invocation (an event) may run (10 000 000).
Calls nested (200).
Bytes of strings and arrays alive (64 MB).

Rlocale_load_csv.doc: Loads a CSV table of translations from a file. Returns the number of keys read, -1 on an error.

Rlocale_set_text.doc: Adds or replaces one text of one language.

Rlocale_get_language_count.doc: Number of languages in the tables, and their codes, in the order of the columns.

Rlocale_set_language.doc:
Chooses the language: an exact code ("pt-BR"), or its first part
("pt") when the tables have no such column. Every widget that shows a key
is updated, and the layout of the windows follows its direction (an
Arabic, Hebrew, Persian or Urdu language is laid out from right to left,
see Rset_layout_direction). Returns R_FALSE when no column matches (the
language is set all the same: the texts fall back).

Rlocale_get_system_language.doc: The language of the user, from the system ("fr-FR", "en-US"...).

Rlocale_set_fallback_language.doc: The language whose texts are shown when the current one has none (default: the first column).

Rlocale_is_rtl.doc: R_TRUE when the language is written from right to left.

Rlocale_set_changed_callback.doc: Called after the language or the tables changed (the widgets are already updated).

Rtr.doc: The text of a key in the current language (see the fallbacks above). Never NULL.

Rtr_exists.doc: R_TRUE when the key has a text in the current language or the fallback one.

Rtr_format.doc:
The text of a key with its {0} {1} ... replaced by the arguments
(translators may put them in any order). "{{" is a brace.

Rtr_plural.doc:
The plural form of a key for a count: the key followed by the CLDR
category of the count in the current language (".zero", ".one", ".two",
".few", ".many", ".other"), else ".other", else the key itself. {n} is
replaced by the count, written in the conventions of the language.

Rwidget_set_text_key.doc:
Makes a widget show a key: an attribute ("Text", "Tooltip",
"Title", "Placeholder"... any attribute that takes a text) is set to the
translation now and every time the language changes. NULL or "" stops it.
Same as Rwidget_set_attribute(widget, attribute, "key").

Rlocale_format_number.doc: A number written in the conventions of the language: decimal separator and digit grouping ("1 234,5" in French).

Raccessibility_set_text_scale.doc: Size of every text, 1 = as designed (0.5 to 4). Controls grow with their text.

Raccessibility_set_high_contrast.doc:
Themes of high contrast: black and white, yellow focus, thick
borders (the dark one, or the light one when the theme in use is light).
R_FALSE goes back to the theme used before.

Raccessibility_set_focus_always_visible.doc: R_TRUE: the focus ring is always shown (not only after the keyboard was used), and thicker.

Raccessibility_set_reduce_motion.doc:
Reduced motion, for the whole application: R_TRUE and nothing
moves by itself. Changes are immediate (no spring, no slide, no bounce,
no transition), and the effects (raven_shader.h) stand still; they still
follow the pointer. Same as Rset_animations_enabled(R_FALSE).

Raccessibility_set_color_filter.doc: A filter on the colors of the interface (pictures and viewports keep theirs).

Raccessibility_follow_system.doc: Applies the settings of the system (text size, contrast, motion).

Rwidget_set_accessible_name.doc: What the screen reader says of the widget; NULL: what it shows (or the label before it).

Rwidget_get_accessible_name.doc: The name the screen reader uses (given, or found). Valid until the next call.

Rwidget_set_accessible_description.doc: A longer explanation, read after the name.

Rwidget_get_accessible_role.doc: The role the screen reader sees (given, or the one of the type).

Rwidget_set_accessible_hidden.doc: R_TRUE: hidden from screen readers, with what it contains (decoration).

Rwidget_set_accessible_labelled_by.doc: The widget is named by another one (a label): its text is the name.

Rwidget_set_accessible_action.doc:
Explicit screen-reader press action, including for custom widgets.
NULL removes the override. Does not change pointer or keyboard handling.
Disabled widgets (including disabled ancestors) cannot be pressed.

Rwidget_set_accessible_checked.doc:
Override the checked state: 1 checked, 0 unchecked, -1 restores the
widget's default (not checkable for a custom widget). The application owns
this state; a press callback updates it when appropriate.

Raccessibility_announce.doc: Has a message read (a save that ended, an error). `assertive`: interrupts what is being read.

Raccessibility_is_screen_reader_active.doc: R_TRUE when a screen reader is reading the windows of the application.

Rvulkan_get_required_instance_extensions.doc:
By default Raven creates its own VkInstance and VkDevice. To make Raven render
with the device of the application (or of HRL), create the instance and the
device with the extensions returned below, then pass them here.

Rvulkan_set_external_device.doc:
Makes Raven use an existing device. Raven does not destroy these objects.
VkInstance
VkPhysicalDevice
VkDevice
VkQueue supporting graphics and presentation
Family index of `queue`

Rvulkan_get_instance.doc: Opaque VkInstance, or NULL before initialization / on another backend.

Rvulkan_get_graphics_queue.doc: Opaque VkQueue used for rendering and presentation.

Rvulkan_simulate_device_lost.doc:
Behaves as if the GPU had answered VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST, to test
how an application recovers (Rset_device_reset_callback). Raven
recovers at the next frame by making a new device: every handle
returned above changes. Does nothing with an external device
(Rvulkan_set_external_device), whose loss the application handles.

Rvulkan_texture_create_from_image_view.doc:
Wraps an application image so that widgets (Image, Viewport) can show it.
The image must be in VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_SHADER_READ_ONLY_OPTIMAL whenever Raven
renders, and must outlive the texture. Raven does not destroy it: destroy it
after Rtexture_destroy, which returns once Raven no longer uses the image.

The values of the image are shown as they are (the UI is not color
managed): use a UNORM view of an sRGB-encoded image. Alpha is honored, so
clear the image with alpha 1 unless the viewport should be see-through.

Raw VkImageView handle (cast to uint64_t).
Raw VkSampler handle, or 0 for the Raven linear sampler.

Rvulkan_texture_set_image_view.doc:
Points an existing wrapped texture to another image view (after a resize).
Returns once Raven no longer uses the previous view, which can then be destroyed.

Rvulkan_texture_create_shared.doc:
Creates an RGBA8 texture whose memory can be imported by another
API or process (OpenGL GL_EXT_memory_object, another Vulkan device).
Requires VK_KHR_external_memory_fd (POSIX) or _win32 (Windows).
Returns R_INVALID_ID when the device cannot export memory.

Rvulkan_texture_get_shared_info.doc: Exports the memory of a shared texture. Each call returns a new handle.

Rbackend_register.doc:
Supplies the backend used by Rinit(R_BACKEND_CUSTOM).
The table is copied. Must be called before Rinit.

Rbackend_device_lost.doc:
Tells Raven that the device of the backend was lost. Thread-safe:
call it from the backend (render thread) when the API reports it. At the
next frame Raven calls Shutdown and Init again, then remakes the
surfaces, the textures and the shaders (see Rset_device_reset_callback).
Until then RenderFrame may simply return.

Rpixels_alloc.doc: Allocates a pixel buffer released by Rpixels_free. Thread-safe.

Rhost_platform_register.doc: Makes the next Rinit use the host platform. The structure is copied; NULL restores the default.

Rhost_platform_is_active.doc: Returns R_TRUE while the running library uses the host platform.

Rhost_window_set_size.doc: Size of a host window in pixels, and pixels per logical unit.

Rhost_window_set_insets.doc:
What covers a host window on a phone or a tablet, in pixels: the
safe area (status bar, notch, home indicator; NULL: none) and the height
of the on-screen keyboard over its bottom (0: hidden). The content is laid
out inside them (Rwindow_get_safe_area, Rwindow_get_keyboard_area).

Rhost_set_system_dark.doc:
The application's system is in dark (R_TRUE) or light (R_FALSE)
mode, -1 when it does not tell (the default): Rtheme_get_system_dark,
and Rtheme_follow_system follows it.

Rhost_inject_mouse_leave.doc: The pointer left the window: hover states end.

Rhost_inject_key.doc: R_TRUE for a key held down (auto-repeat).

Rhost_inject_composition.doc:
The input method of the application's system composes `text`
(preedit), with its selection in bytes (see Rwindow_inject_composition).
NULL or "" cancels it; the committed text then comes through
Rhost_inject_text. Rwindow_get_text_input_rect tells where to put the
candidate window.

Rhost_inject_focus.doc: The window gained or lost the keyboard. Losing it closes popups and drops captures.

Rhost_inject_close.doc: The user asked to close the window (its close callback decides).

Rtest_set_deterministic.doc:
R_TRUE makes what is drawn depend only on what the test does:
every frame advances the animations by 1/60 s (Rset_animation_time_step),
and the carets of the text fields stay lit instead of blinking. R_FALSE
gives the clock back (time step 0).

Rtest_get_platform_tag.doc:
Returns What the goldens of this run are made with, "OS-backend":
"macos-metal", "linux-vulkan", "windows-vulkan", "web-webgl"... and
"null" with the null backend.

Rtest_find.doc:
Finds a widget by name (Rwidget_set_name, Name="" in XML). The
path may have several names separated by '/': "settings/ok" is the
widget named "ok" inside the one named "settings". In a window, the
open popups (menus, dialogs) are searched first, top first, then the
content.
A window or a widget.
Returns R_INVALID_ID when nothing has that name (no error is reported).

Rtest_click.doc: Moves the mouse to the middle of the widget, presses and releases the left button.

Rtest_double_click.doc: Two clicks in a row on the middle of the widget, seen as a double click.

Rtest_right_click.doc: A click of the right button on the middle of the widget (a context menu).

Rtest_click_at.doc:
Clicks at a position of a widget or a window.
1 for a click, 2 for a double click, 3 for a triple click.
RModifier held during the clicks (R_MOD_SHIFT...).

Rtest_hover.doc: Moves the mouse over the middle of the widget, without clicking.

Rtest_hover_at.doc: Moves the mouse to a position of a widget or a window.

Rtest_drag.doc:
Presses the left button on the middle of the widget, moves by
(dx, dy) in several steps, and releases: a slider, a splitter, a
window dragged by a widget.

Rtest_drag_to.doc: Drags from the middle of one widget to the middle of another (drag and drop).

Rtest_scroll.doc:
Turns the mouse wheel over the middle of the widget: `wheel_y`
notches (positive: toward the top, as a wheel turned away from the
user), `wheel_x` notches sideways.

Rtest_key.doc:
Presses and releases a key, with RModifier held. A widget
target gets the keyboard focus first; a window sends the key to what
has the focus.

Rtest_type_text.doc:
Types UTF-8 text as a keyboard would. A widget target gets the
keyboard focus first. '\n', '\t' and '\b' are sent as the keys Enter,
Tab and Backspace.

Rtest_tap.doc: A finger touches the middle of the widget and leaves at once.

Rtest_swipe.doc:
A finger put on the middle of the widget moves by (dx, dy) in
`seconds`, and leaves: a fast swipe flicks a list, which then coasts
(Rtest_settle lets it stop).

Rtest_pump.doc: Produces `frames` frames (Rdraw_frame). return R_FALSE once the application quits.

Rtest_is_idle.doc:
Returns R_TRUE when nothing waits for a frame: no posted task, no layout
to do, nothing to paint, no animation, no layout spring, no inertia.
Windows that redraw all the time (Rwindow_set_continuous_redraw, a
realtime viewport) and the timers are not counted.

Rtest_settle.doc:
Produces frames until Rtest_is_idle, each advancing the
animations by the time step (1/60 s unless Rset_animation_time_step
gives another), for at most `max_seconds` of that time.
Returns R_FALSE when it was still moving at the end.

Rtest_get_text.doc:
Returns What the user reads in the widget: the text of a field, else
its label (as screen readers say it: the text of a Label, a Button, a
Checkbox...). "" when it has none. Valid until the next call.

Rtest_is_shown.doc:
Returns R_TRUE when the widget can be seen: in a window, Visible with
all that holds it, on the page a Switcher or a TabView shows, and laid
out with a size.

Rtest_is_checked.doc: Returns R_TRUE for a checked Checkbox, Switch, RadioButton, toggle Button or menu item.

Rtest_expect_golden.doc:
Captures a window, or the rectangle of one widget, and compares
it with the PNG file `golden_path` (see the top of this file).
A window or a widget.
NULL for the defaults.
Receives the details; may be NULL.
Returns R_TRUE when the capture matches (or the golden was written
because RAVEN_UPDATE_GOLDENS=1).

Rtest_compare_pixels.doc:
Compares two RGBA8 images of the same size as Rtest_expect_golden
does, without files.
When not NULL, receives width * height * 4 bytes: the
expected image faded, with the different pixels in red.
Returns The number of pixels farther apart than `channel_tolerance`;
-1 when an image is missing.
